#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding()]
param()

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$scriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
. (Join-Path $scriptDir 'plugin-env.ps1')
. (Join-Path $scriptDir 'resolve-cache-dir.ps1')

$cacheDir = Resolve-McpCacheDir
$sessionFile = Join-Path $cacheDir 'session-state.yaml'
$turnFile = Join-Path $cacheDir 'current-turn.yaml'
$pendingDir = Join-Path $cacheDir 'pending'
$namespaces = @(
    'workflow.sessionlog'
    'workflow.todo'
    'workflow.requirements'
    'workflow.triage'
    'workflow.graphrag'
    'workflow.memory'
    'workflow.failsafe'
)
$requirementMethods = @(
    'workflow.requirements.listLayers'
    'workflow.requirements.createLayer'
    'workflow.requirements.updateLayer'
    'workflow.requirements.effective'
    'workflow.requirements.planRecovery'
    'workflow.requirements.applyRecovery'
    'workflow.requirements.getRecovery'
)
$requirementClientMethods = @(
    'client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync'
    'client.Requirements.CreateRequirementLayerAsync'
    'client.Requirements.UpdateRequirementLayerAsync'
    'client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync'
    'client.Requirements.PlanRecoveryAsync'
    'client.Requirements.ApplyRecoveryAsync'
    'client.Requirements.GetRecoveryAsync'
)

function Test-McpStatusSessionState {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path)

    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return $false }

    try {
        $statusLine = Select-String -LiteralPath $Path -Pattern '^status:\s*verified\s*$' | Select-Object -First 1
        if (-not $statusLine) { return $false }

        $sessionLine = Select-String -LiteralPath $Path -Pattern '^sessionId:\s*(?<value>.+)$' | Select-Object -First 1
        if (-not $sessionLine) { return $false }

        $sessionId = [string]$sessionLine.Matches[0].Groups['value'].Value
        $sessionId = $sessionId.Trim().Trim('''').Trim('"')
        return -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($sessionId)
    } catch {
        return $false
    }
}

function Measure-McpStatusYamlFile {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        TR-MCP-REPL-017: counts YAML records directly inside one directory.
    .DESCRIPTION
        Returns 0 for a missing directory. Not recursive, so the quarantine
        subdirectory is never folded into the live queue depth.
    .PARAMETER Path
        Directory to count.
    #>
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][AllowEmptyString()][string]$Path)

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Path)) { return 0 }
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path -PathType Container)) { return 0 }
    return @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Path -Filter '*.yaml' -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Count
}

# TR-MCP-REPL-017 (BUG-TRIAGE-097): the failsafe queue is real pending work. Status
# used to report only the 'pending' directory, so it printed pendingCount 0 while
# captured session submits sat undrained on disk.
$failsafeDir = try { Get-McpFailsafeDir } catch { '' }
$quarantineDir = try { Get-McpFailsafeQuarantineDir } catch { '' }
$pendingTurnCount = Measure-McpStatusYamlFile -Path $pendingDir
$failsafeCount = Measure-McpStatusYamlFile -Path $failsafeDir
$quarantineCount = Measure-McpStatusYamlFile -Path $quarantineDir

$hasSession = Test-McpStatusSessionState -Path $sessionFile
$status = [ordered]@{
    status = if ($hasSession) { 'available' } else { 'no-session' }
    agent = $env:MCP_AGENT_NAME
    namespaces = $namespaces
    requirementMethods = $requirementMethods
    requirementClientMethods = $requirementClientMethods
    cacheDir = $cacheDir
    hasSession = $hasSession
    hasCurrentTurn = Test-Path -LiteralPath $turnFile
    pendingCount = $pendingTurnCount + $failsafeCount
    pendingTurnCount = $pendingTurnCount
    failsafeDir = $failsafeDir
    failsafeCount = $failsafeCount
    failsafeQuarantineCount = $quarantineCount
}

$status | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Resolve the workspace-scoped PowerShell plugin cache directory.
.DESCRIPTION
    Runtime state belongs to the active workspace, never to the installed
    plugin checkout. The returned path is <workspace>/.mcpServer/<agent>.

    Precedence:
      1. MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE for an explicit test or recovery override.
      2. The workspace marker found from the explicit or active start path.
      3. MCP/host workspace environment variables as a markerless fallback.
 #>

$script:ResolveCacheDirScriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path

function Get-McpCacheAgentKey {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()

    # FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002: inherited Grok variables must not move a Codex
    # plugin into the Grok cache namespace.
    $inheritedAgent = @($env:PLUGIN_AGENT_NAME, $env:MCP_AGENT_NAME) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($env:MCP_PLUGIN_HOST -match '^(?i:codex)$' -and $inheritedAgent -match '(?i)grok') {
        return 'codex'
    }

    $agent = @(
        $env:MCP_AGENT_NAME,
        $env:PLUGIN_AGENT_NAME,
        $env:PLUGIN_AGENT_DEFAULT,
        $env:MCP_PLUGIN_HOST
    ) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) } | Select-Object -First 1

    if (-not $agent) { return 'default' }

    switch ($agent.Trim().ToLowerInvariant()) {
        'claude' { return 'claude' }
        'claudecode' { return 'claude' }
        'claude-code' { return 'claude' }
        'claudecowork' { return 'cowork' }
        'claude-cowork' { return 'cowork' }
        'codex' { return 'codex' }
        'copilot' { return 'copilot' }
        'grok' { return 'grok' }
        'grokcode' { return 'grok' }
        'grok-code' { return 'grok' }
        'cline' { return 'cline' }
        'cline-v2' { return 'cline' }
        'opencode' { return 'opencode' }
        'open-code' { return 'opencode' }
    }

    $key = ($agent.Trim() -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9]+', '-').Trim('-').ToLowerInvariant()
    if (-not $key) { return 'default' }
    return $key
}

function Get-McpPluginRoot {
    if ($env:MCP_PLUGIN_ROOT) { return $env:MCP_PLUGIN_ROOT }
    if ($env:CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT) { return $env:CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT }
    return (Split-Path -Parent $script:ResolveCacheDirScriptDir)
}

function Join-McpWorkspaceCachePath {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$WorkspacePath)

    return (Join-Path (Join-Path $WorkspacePath '.mcpServer') (Get-McpCacheAgentKey))
}

function Get-McpBackgroundScopeKey {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        TR-MCP-PLUGIN-013 AC-005 (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 D3): the identity of a background host: MCP_SUBAGENT_ID, else GROK_SUBAGENT_ID,
        else the hook payload's session_id. None when there is none or when it equals the agentSessionId recorded for the root, because
        then the prompt is the root host's own.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [string]$PayloadSessionId,
        [string]$RootAgentSessionId
    )

    $key = @($env:MCP_SUBAGENT_ID, $env:GROK_SUBAGENT_ID, $PayloadSessionId) |
        Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($key)) { return $null }
    $key = $key.Trim()
    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($RootAgentSessionId) -and
        [string]::Equals($key, $RootAgentSessionId.Trim(), [System.StringComparison]::Ordinal)) {
        return $null
    }
    return $key
}

function Join-McpBackgroundScopePath {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        TR-MCP-PLUGIN-013 AC-005 (D3): the cache folder of one background host, <cache>/background/<key>. A key with characters other than
        letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen, or longer than 96 characters, is made file-safe and suffixed with a hash of the
        original, so two keys never share a folder.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$CacheDir,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Key
    )

    $safe = ($Key -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+', '-').Trim('-', '.')
    if ($safe -cne $Key -or $safe.Length -gt 96) {
        $hash = [System.Convert]::ToHexString([System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::HashData([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($Key))).Substring(0, 12).ToLowerInvariant()
        if ($safe.Length -gt 80) { $safe = $safe.Substring(0, 80) }
        $safe = if ($safe) { "$safe-$hash" } else { $hash }
    }
    return (Join-Path (Join-Path $CacheDir 'background') $safe)
}

function Resolve-McpBackgroundScopeCacheDir {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        TR-MCP-PLUGIN-013 AC-005 (D3): the cache a session-log verb the agent calls itself uses. With no MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE and with
        MCP_SUBAGENT_ID or GROK_SUBAGENT_ID set, that agent's background folder when it holds a current-turn.yaml; otherwise CacheDir.
        Those two are the only host identities an agent's own calls carry.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$CacheDir)

    if ($env:MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE) { return $CacheDir }
    $key = @($env:MCP_SUBAGENT_ID, $env:GROK_SUBAGENT_ID) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($key)) { return $CacheDir }
    $scope = Join-McpBackgroundScopePath -CacheDir $CacheDir -Key $key.Trim()
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $scope 'current-turn.yaml') -PathType Leaf) { return $scope }
    return $CacheDir
}

function Get-McpWorkspaceFromEnvironment {
    $configured = @(
        $env:MCPSERVER_WORKSPACE_PATH,
        $env:MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH,
        $env:CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR,
        $env:CODEX_WORKSPACE_PATH,
        $env:CODEX_PROJECT_DIR,
        $env:COWORK_WORKSPACE_PATH,
        $env:CLINE_WORKSPACE_PATH,
        $env:OPENCODE_WORKSPACE_PATH
    ) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) } | Select-Object -First 1

    if ($configured -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $configured -PathType Container)) {
        return (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $configured).ProviderPath
    }

    return $null
}

function Resolve-McpCacheDir {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$StartPath)

    if ($env:MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE) {
        return $env:MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE
    }

    if (-not (Get-Command Find-MarkerFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        $resolver = Join-Path $script:ResolveCacheDirScriptDir 'marker-resolver.ps1'
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $resolver) {
            . $resolver
        }
    }

    $explicitWorkspace = @(
        $env:MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH,
        $env:MCPSERVER_WORKSPACE_PATH,
        $env:CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
    ) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ -PathType Container) } | Select-Object -First 1

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($StartPath) -and $explicitWorkspace) {
        return (Join-McpWorkspaceCachePath -WorkspacePath ((Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $explicitWorkspace).ProviderPath))
    }

    $startCandidates = if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($StartPath)) {
        @($StartPath)
    } else {
        @(
            $env:CODEX_CWD,
            (Get-Location).Path
        ) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) } | Select-Object -Unique
    }

    if (Get-Command Find-MarkerFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        foreach ($startDir in $startCandidates) {
            try {
                $markerFile = Find-MarkerFile -StartDir $startDir
                if ($markerFile) {
                    return (Join-McpWorkspaceCachePath -WorkspacePath (Split-Path -Parent $markerFile))
                }
            } catch {
                # Try the next active start candidate, then configured env.
            }
        }
    }

    $configuredWorkspace = Get-McpWorkspaceFromEnvironment
    if ($configuredWorkspace) {
        return (Join-McpWorkspaceCachePath -WorkspacePath $configuredWorkspace)
    }

    throw "Unable to resolve the active workspace cache. Set MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH or MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE; plugin install paths are not workspace caches."
}

function Get-McpFailsafeFileSha256Hex {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        SHA-256 of a file as uppercase hex, used for failsafe queue migration.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path)

    $sha = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create()
    try {
        $stream = [System.IO.File]::OpenRead($Path)
        try {
            $hash = $sha.ComputeHash($stream)
            return (([BitConverter]::ToString($hash) -replace '-', ''))
        } finally {
            $stream.Dispose()
        }
    } finally {
        $sha.Dispose()
    }
}

function Get-McpFailsafeAgentSegment {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Agent path segment matching FilesystemSessionLogPersistenceStrategy.SanitizePathSegment.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()

    $inheritedAgent = @($env:PLUGIN_AGENT_NAME, $env:MCP_AGENT_NAME) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($env:MCP_PLUGIN_HOST -match '^(?i:codex)$' -and $inheritedAgent -match 'grok') {
        $agent = 'Codex'
    } else {
        $agent = @(
            $env:PLUGIN_AGENT_NAME,
            $env:MCP_AGENT_NAME,
            $env:PLUGIN_AGENT_DEFAULT,
            $env:MCP_PLUGIN_HOST
        ) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) } | Select-Object -First 1
    }

    if (-not $agent) {
        return (Get-McpCacheAgentKey)
    }

    $builder = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder
    foreach ($character in $agent.ToCharArray()) {
        if ([char]::IsLetterOrDigit($character) -or $character -eq '-' -or $character -eq '_' -or $character -eq '.') {
            [void]$builder.Append($character)
        } else {
            [void]$builder.Append('_')
        }
    }

    $result = $builder.ToString().Trim('.')
    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($result)) { return 'unknown' }
    return $result
}

function Get-McpFailsafeWorkspaceKey {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Workspace key matching FilesystemSessionLogPersistenceStrategy (base64url of UTF-8 full path).
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$WorkspacePath)

    $full = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($WorkspacePath)
    $bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($full)
    $b64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes)
    return (($b64 -replace '\+', '-') -replace '/', '_').TrimEnd('=')
}

function Resolve-McpFailsafeWorkspacePath {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Resolves the workspace root used for the V4 failsafe tree.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$StartPath)

    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($StartPath) -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $StartPath -PathType Container)) {
        return [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($StartPath)
    }

    $configured = Get-McpWorkspaceFromEnvironment
    if ($configured) { return $configured }

    if (Get-Command Find-MarkerFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $startCandidates = if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($StartPath)) { @($StartPath) } else {
            @(
                $env:MCP_WORKSPACE_START_DIR,
                $env:MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH,
                $env:MCPSERVER_WORKSPACE_PATH,
                (Get-Location).Path
            ) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($_) } | Select-Object -Unique
        }
        foreach ($startDir in $startCandidates) {
            try {
                $markerFile = Find-MarkerFile -StartDir $startDir
                if ($markerFile) {
                    return [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Split-Path -Parent $markerFile))
                }
            } catch {
            }
        }
    }

    throw "Unable to resolve the workspace root for the V4 failsafe queue. Set MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH or MCPSERVER_FAILSAFE_DIR."
}

function Invoke-McpFailsafeLegacyQueueMigration {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Copy-then-delete legacy plugin failsafe YAML into the V4 pending directory after SHA-256 match.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$WorkspacePath,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$PendingDir
    )

    $mcpRoot = Join-Path $WorkspacePath '.mcpServer'
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $mcpRoot -PathType Container)) {
        return
    }

    [void][System.IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($PendingDir)

    $legacyDirs = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    foreach ($child in [System.IO.Directory]::GetDirectories($mcpRoot)) {
        $name = [System.IO.Path]::GetFileName($child)
        if ([string]::Equals($name, 'failsafe', [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
            continue
        }

        $legacy = Join-Path $child 'failsafe'
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $legacy -PathType Container) {
            $legacyDirs.Add($legacy)
        }
    }

    foreach ($legacy in $legacyDirs) {
        $files = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $legacy -File -Filter '*.yaml' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)
        foreach ($file in $files) {
            $dest = Join-Path $PendingDir $file.Name
            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dest)) {
                Copy-Item -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Destination $dest -Force
            }

            if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dest) {
                $sourceHash = Get-McpFailsafeFileSha256Hex -Path $file.FullName
                $destHash = Get-McpFailsafeFileSha256Hex -Path $dest
                if ($sourceHash -eq $destHash) {
                    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $file.FullName -Force
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

function Get-McpFailsafeDir {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        TR-MCP-REPL-016: resolves the V4 failsafe pending directory.
    .DESCRIPTION
        Single source of truth for the queue location so the writer (repl-invoke),
        the drain, and the status reporter all agree with
        FilesystemSessionLogPersistenceStrategy:
        {workspace}/.mcpServer/failsafe/{agent}/workspaces/{workspace-key}/pending/.
        MCPSERVER_FAILSAFE_DIR and MCP_FAILSAFE_DIR override for tests and recovery.
        Legacy {workspace}/.mcpServer/{agent}/failsafe YAML is migrated by checksum
        match then source delete.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$StartPath)

    if ($env:MCPSERVER_FAILSAFE_DIR) { return $env:MCPSERVER_FAILSAFE_DIR }
    if ($env:MCP_FAILSAFE_DIR) { return $env:MCP_FAILSAFE_DIR }

    # FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003: a cache override is the supported markerless
    # recovery target. Keep the write-ahead queue beside it when no workspace
    # root can be resolved, so title and submit calls are not reported lost
    # before the server is attempted. An explicit failsafe override above
    # still wins, including a non-directory used to prove a lost write.
    try {
        $workspace = Resolve-McpFailsafeWorkspacePath -StartPath $StartPath
    } catch {
        $override = $env:MCP_CACHE_DIR_OVERRIDE
        if ($override -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $override -PathType Container)) {
            $overridePending = Join-Path $override 'failsafe-pending'
            [void][System.IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($overridePending)
            return $overridePending
        }

        throw
    }
    $agent = Get-McpFailsafeAgentSegment
    $key = Get-McpFailsafeWorkspaceKey -WorkspacePath $workspace
    $pending = Join-Path $workspace (Join-Path '.mcpServer' (Join-Path 'failsafe' (Join-Path $agent (Join-Path 'workspaces' (Join-Path $key 'pending')))))
    [void][System.IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($pending)
    Invoke-McpFailsafeLegacyQueueMigration -WorkspacePath $workspace -PendingDir $pending
    return $pending
}

function Get-McpFailsafeQuarantineDir {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        TR-MCP-REPL-017: resolves the quarantine directory under the failsafe queue.
    .DESCRIPTION
        Records that cannot be replayed are moved here instead of being deleted or
        retried forever, so nothing is lost and the live queue keeps draining.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([string]$StartPath)

    return (Join-Path (Get-McpFailsafeDir -StartPath $StartPath) 'quarantine')
}

function Get-McpPathVolumeRoot {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        FR-MCP-TEMPVOL-001: returns the volume root of a filesystem path.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path)

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($Path)) { return $null }

    try {
        $full = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Path)
        $root = [System.IO.Path]::GetPathRoot($full)
        if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($root)) { return $null }
        return $root
    } catch {
        return $null
    }
}

    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        FR-MCP-TEMPVOL-001: builds the TEMP alignment result object.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [bool]$Succeeded,
        [bool]$Changed,

function Get-McpPluginWorkspaceTempDirectory {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        FR-MCP-TEMPVOL-001: prefers workspace .mcpServer/tmp on the target volume.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$TargetPath)

    $dir = $TargetPath
    $isLeaf = $false
    try {
        $isLeaf = Test-Path -LiteralPath $TargetPath -PathType Leaf
    } catch {
        $isLeaf = $false
    }
    if ($isLeaf) {
        $dir = Split-Path -Parent $TargetPath
    }

    $cursor = $dir
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 20 -and -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($cursor); $i++) {
        $marker = Join-Path $cursor 'AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml'
        $markerExists = $false
        try {
            $markerExists = Test-Path -LiteralPath $marker -PathType Leaf
        } catch {
            $markerExists = $false
        }
        if ($markerExists) {
            return (Join-Path (Join-Path $cursor '.mcpServer') 'tmp')
        }

        $parent = Split-Path -Parent $cursor
        if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($parent) -or $parent -eq $cursor) { break }
        $cursor = $parent
    }

    return (Join-Path (Join-Path $dir '.mcpServer') 'tmp')
}

function Set-McpPluginSameVolumeTemp {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        FR-MCP-TEMPVOL-001 / TR-MCP-TEMPVOL-001: align process TEMP and TMP to the target volume.
    .DESCRIPTION
        When TEMP/TMP are on a different volume than TargetPath, sets both to a writable
        directory on the target volume. Same-volume TEMP is left unchanged. A failed
        directory create does not mutate TEMP/TMP and returns Succeeded false with Error.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$TargetPath)

    $currentTemp = if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($env:TEMP)) {
        $env:TEMP
    } elseif (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($env:TMP)) {
        $env:TMP
    } else {
        [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()
    }

    $targetRoot = Get-McpPathVolumeRoot -Path $TargetPath
    $tempRoot = Get-McpPathVolumeRoot -Path $currentTemp
    if ($targetRoot -and $tempRoot -and $targetRoot.Equals($tempRoot, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
        return (New-McpPluginTempAlignmentResult -Succeeded $true -Changed $false -TempPath $currentTemp)
    }

    try {
        $alignedDir = Get-McpPluginWorkspaceTempDirectory -TargetPath $TargetPath
        [void][System.IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory($alignedDir)
        $probe = Join-Path $alignedDir ('.write-probe-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
        [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($probe, 'ok')
        [System.IO.File]::Delete($probe)
    } catch {
        return (New-McpPluginTempAlignmentResult -Succeeded $false -Changed $false -TempPath $currentTemp -ErrorMessage ('Unable to create writable TEMP on the workspace volume: ' + $_.Exception.Message))
    }

    $resolved = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($alignedDir)
    $env:TEMP = $resolved
    $env:TMP = $resolved
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('TEMP', $resolved, 'Process')
    [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('TMP', $resolved, 'Process')
    return (New-McpPluginTempAlignmentResult -Succeeded $true -Changed $true -TempPath $resolved)
}

function Invoke-McpPluginReplacementMove {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        FR-MCP-TEMPVOL-001: replacement move that never reports success when the destination is unchanged.
    .DESCRIPTION
        Cross-volume File.Move is refused with a visible Error. Exceptions and missing
        destinations also return Succeeded false. Preview-without-apply cannot look like success.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$SourcePath,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$DestinationPath
    )

    $failed = {
        param([string]$Message)
        return [pscustomobject]@{
            Succeeded = $false
            Error = $Message
            DestinationUnchanged = $true
        }
    }

    $srcRoot = $null
    $dstRoot = $null
    try { $srcRoot = Get-McpPathVolumeRoot -Path $SourcePath } catch { $srcRoot = $null }
    try { $dstRoot = Get-McpPathVolumeRoot -Path $DestinationPath } catch { $dstRoot = $null }

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($srcRoot) -or [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($dstRoot)) {
        return (& $failed 'replacement move refused: source or destination volume could not be resolved')
    }

    if (-not $srcRoot.Equals($dstRoot, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
        return (& $failed 'cross-volume replacement move refused: TEMP/TMP must be on the destination volume')
    }

    try {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $SourcePath -PathType Leaf)) {
            return (& $failed 'replacement move failed: source file is missing')
        }

        $destDir = Split-Path -Parent $DestinationPath
        if ($destDir -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $destDir -PathType Container)) {
            return (& $failed 'replacement move failed: destination directory is missing')
        }

        [System.IO.File]::Move($SourcePath, $DestinationPath, $true)
    } catch {
        return (& $failed ('replacement move failed: ' + $_.Exception.Message))
    }

    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $DestinationPath -PathType Leaf)) {
        return (& $failed 'replacement move failed: destination is missing after move')
    }

    return [pscustomobject]@{
        Succeeded = $true
        Error = $null
        DestinationUnchanged = $false
    }
}

# (the plugin keeps a failsafe YAML when the server cannot accept it), then report the failsafe queue depth.
[CmdletBinding()]
param()
Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$plugin = '[HOME]/github/mcpserver-claude-code-plugin'
$ws = '[HOME]/github/WordGame/.mcpServer/wordpairs'
$wrapper = Join-Path $plugin 'lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1'
Set-Location -LiteralPath $ws
Import-Module (Join-Path $plugin 'lib/McpPluginShim.psm1') -Force
$evidence = @(
    'marker signature: valid (plugin Test-MarkerSignature)',
    'plugin Invoke-FullBootstrap: 5 attempts 2026-10-28T23:04:56..23:09:29 local, each "HttpClient.Timeout of 5 seconds elapsing"',
    'direct marker /health nonce check with 90 s client timeout at 2026-10-28T23:07:33 local: timed out',
    'server pid 597684 from marker is alive (/proc entry present)',
    'UserPromptSubmit hook for this reviewer prompt ended outcome=cancelled exit_code=1 (response.jsonl line 6)'
) -join '; '
$params = New-McpTriageReportParams `
    -Title 'MCP server /health hangs; plugin trust bootstrap times out' `
    -Summary 'The wordpairs workspace MCP server process is alive but GET /health?nonce=... does not answer within 5 s or 90 s, so marker trust fails (MCP_UNTRUSTED) and a hostile-validation reviewer cannot load memories, read QBrain or write its required session-log turn.' `
    -Component 'McpServer' `
    -AffectedPaths @('AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml', 'lib/marker-resolver.ps1') `
    -AffectedSymbols @('/health', 'Invoke-FullBootstrap') `
    -ErrorSignature 'health_timeout_mcp_untrusted' `
    -DedupeKey 'wordpairs-health-timeout-20261028' `
    -Evidence $evidence `
    -ReporterAgent 'ClaudeCode' `
    -WorkspacePath $ws `
    -ReproductionHints @('pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File docs/receipts/hv/claude-opus-round3-tools/R3-01b-HealthLong.ps1') `
    -Tags @('hostile-validation', 'mcp-untrusted', 'health-timeout')
$started = Get-Date
$out = ''
try {
    $out = (& $wrapper -Command Invoke -Method 'workflow.triage.report' -ParamsObject $params -WorkspacePath $ws -PluginRoot $plugin 2>&1 | Out-String)
} catch {
    $out = 'WRAPPER-ERROR: ' + $_.Exception.Message
}
$out = [regex]::Replace($out, '(?i)(api[_-]?key["'':\s=]+)[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}', '$1<redacted>')
Write-Output ("TRIAGE at {0} elapsedMs={1}" -f $started.ToString('s'), [int]((Get-Date) - $started).TotalMilliseconds)
Write-Output ($out.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(3000, $out.Length)))
$status = & $wrapper -Command Status -WorkspacePath $ws -PluginRoot $plugin 2>&1 | Out-String
$st = $status | ConvertFrom-Json
Write-Output ("FAILSAFE: count={0} pending={1} quarantine={2}" -f $st.failsafeCount, $st.pendingCount, $st.failsafeQuarantineCount)
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $st.failsafeDir) { Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $st.failsafeDir -File | ForEach-Object { Write-Output ("  FAILSAFE-FILE {0} {1}" -f $_.Name, $_.LastWriteTime.ToString('s')) } }

178	    # Method that should be replayed from the failsafe record.
179	    [string]$Method
180	
181	    # Human-readable queue label used in the failsafe filename.
182	    [string]$Label
183	
184	    # UTC timestamp string written into the failsafe document.
185	    [string]$Timestamp
186	
187	    # YAML or JSON payload body indented under params.

193	    McpPluginFailsafeRecord([string]$method, [string]$label, [string]$timestamp, [string]$paramsYaml, [string]$path) {
194	        $this.Method = $method
195	        $this.Label = $label
196	        $this.Timestamp = $timestamp
197	        $this.ParamsYaml = $paramsYaml
198	        $this.Path = $path
199	    }
200	
201	    [string] ToYaml() {
202	        # Build the record as an object and serialize it; ParamsYaml is deserialized so the
203	        # params land as a nested mapping, never as re-indented text.
204	        if (-not (Get-Command ConvertFrom-Yaml -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
205	            Import-Module powershell-yaml -ErrorAction Stop
206	        }
207	        $params = $null
208	        if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($this.ParamsYaml)) {
209	            $params = ConvertFrom-Yaml -Yaml $this.ParamsYaml -Ordered
210	        }
211	        if ($null -eq $params) { $params = [ordered]@{} }
212	        $document = [ordered]@{
213	            method = $this.Method
214	            label = $this.Label
215	            timestamp = $this.Timestamp
216	            params = $params
217	        }
218	        return (ConvertTo-McpPluginYaml -InputObject $document)

function New-McpTriageReportParams {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Creates object-safe params for workflow.triage.report.
    .DESCRIPTION
        Returns an ordered PowerShell map that can be passed to Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1
        with -ParamsObject or to New-McpPluginReplRequest -Params. This avoids
        handwritten YAML while preserving the workflow.triage.report contract.

        Members:
        Title - Short problem statement.
        Summary - Observed failure and why it matters.
        Component - Product area, package, or plugin name.
        AffectedPaths - Relevant file paths when known.
        AffectedSymbols - Relevant methods, commands, or API names when known.
        ErrorSignature - Stable error text, status code, or exception type.
        DedupeKey - Stable key for repeated reports.
        Evidence - Compact command output or reproduction context.
        ReporterAgent - Real submitting agent identity.
    .EXAMPLE
        $params = New-McpTriageReportParams -Title 'Plugin wrapper hides errors' -Summary 'workflow.triage.report failures are not visible.' -Component mcpserver-plugin -ReporterAgent Codex
        ./lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method workflow.triage.report -ParamsObject $params
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Title,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Summary,
        [string]$Component = '',
        [string[]]$AffectedPaths = @(),
        [string[]]$AffectedSymbols = @(),
        [string]$ErrorSignature = '',
        [string]$DedupeKey = '',
        [string]$Evidence = '',
        [string]$ReporterAgent = '',
        [string]$WorkspacePath = '',
        [string]$SessionId = '',
        [string]$TurnId = '',
        [string]$CurrentTodoId = '',
        [string[]]$ReproductionHints = @(),
        [string[]]$Tags = @(),
        [string]$IdempotencyKey = ''
    )

    $params = [ordered]@{
        title = $Title
        summary = $Summary
    }

    foreach ($entry in @(
        @{ Name = 'component'; Value = $Component },
        @{ Name = 'errorSignature'; Value = $ErrorSignature },
        @{ Name = 'dedupeKey'; Value = $DedupeKey },
        @{ Name = 'evidence'; Value = $Evidence },
        @{ Name = 'reporterAgent'; Value = $ReporterAgent },
        @{ Name = 'workspacePath'; Value = $WorkspacePath },
        @{ Name = 'sessionId'; Value = $SessionId },
        @{ Name = 'turnId'; Value = $TurnId },
        @{ Name = 'currentTodoId'; Value = $CurrentTodoId },
        @{ Name = 'idempotencyKey'; Value = $IdempotencyKey }
    )) {
        if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$entry.Value)) {
            $params[$entry.Name] = [string]$entry.Value
        }
    }

    foreach ($entry in @(
        @{ Name = 'affectedPaths'; Value = $AffectedPaths },
        @{ Name = 'affectedSymbols'; Value = $AffectedSymbols },
        @{ Name = 'reproductionHints'; Value = $ReproductionHints },
        @{ Name = 'tags'; Value = $Tags }
    )) {
        $values = @(@($entry.Value) | Where-Object { -not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace([string]$_) })
        if ($values.Count -gt 0) {
            $params[$entry.Name] = [string[]]$values
        }
    }

    return $params
}

1	# Guest game and GitHub admin PWA release
2	
3	Current operator scope, 28 October 2026. This document supersedes the public
4	OpenAI sign-in, public PWA installation and browser role-delegation portions of
5	the earlier designs. QBrain is authoritative; this is its linked implementation
6	and verification projection. Implementation and hosted rollout are in progress.
7	
8	## Behavior and boundaries
9	
10	The public game accepts guests only. Generated aliases, icons, browser-persistent
11	guest credentials, rooms, private live updates and reactions remain available.
12	Public OpenAI login/callback routes return404. Public session responses expose no
13	administration permissions, stored/bootstrap grants do not elevate guests, and
14	member-shaped public sessions are rejected. Community suggestion/nomination UI
15	and the former `/content` entry are inactive in this release.
16	
17	Administration uses the registered [Word Pairs Admin GitHub App](https://github.com/settings/apps/word-pairs-admin-sharpninja).
18	Only verified GitHub numeric account16146732 and login `sharpninja` can complete
19	sign-in. The private App requests no repository, organization or email permissions
20	and has no webhook. User-access delegation is disabled: `/admin/users` redirects
21	to `/admin` and its API returns404 without touching access storage. Existing ACL
22	and community policy/domain/history remain preserved for future scope.
23	
24	Server configuration uses `WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and
25	`WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, never public-prefixed variables. Both callback
26	URLs are registered exactly:
27	
28	- `https://wordpairs.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (staging).
29	- `https://wordpairs-j9jf.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (production).
30	
31	The provider uses Authorization Code with S256PKCE and state. Existing persisted
32	challenges are browser-bound, expire after10minutes and are consumed before
33	callback validation. The server exchanges the code and verifies `/user`; it
34	retains neither GitHub access/refresh tokens nor provider email. Admin cookies
35	`wp_admin`/`wp_admin_login` and stored hashes have a separate `github-admin` purpose
36	namespace from `wp_session`. Copying a guest token into an admin cookie or the
37	reverse cannot authenticate. Admin login/logout leaves the guest session intact.
38	Admin responses are private/no-store; logout requires the canonical same origin.
39	
40	## Installation and offline behavior
41	
42	Only the admin layout links `/admin/manifest.webmanifest`. Its stable identity,
43	start URL and scope are `/admin`; display is standalone and its name is Wordpairs
44	Admin. Existing opaque192/512 PNGs, maskable icon and Apple touch icon are reused.
45	The manifest is an explicit route because nested `admin/manifest.ts` is not a
46	recognized metadata convention in the installed Next.js version.
47	
48	Authenticated admin UI offers installation and phone instructions. It registers
49	`/admin-sw.js` with scope `/admin`, `updateViaCache: none`, no-store script headers
50	and `Service-Worker-Allowed: /admin`. The worker handles only same-origin GET
51	admin document navigation. HTTP errors pass through; a network failure receives
52	the generic `/admin-offline.html` reconnect/sign-in screen. API/auth/RSC requests,
53	mutations and public game navigation receive no offline fallback. No operation
54	is queued for later execution.
55	
56	Only the offline document and four public icons are cached under
57	`wordpairs-admin-pwa-v1`. Sessions, profiles, admin HTML, answers, room projections,
58	credentials and mutation responses are never put in CacheStorage. Normal admin
59	updates wait for active clients and delete only older admin cache versions.
60	
61	Public pages have no manifest or install controls. The former `/sw.js` remains
62	as a retirement worker with no fetch handler; it deletes only `wordpairs-pwa-*`
63	caches and unregisters itself. Root cleanup recognizes only that exact former
64	root registration and cache prefix, preserving admin and unrelated apps. Website
65	code cannot remove an existing OS home-screen icon or prevent browser bookmarks.
66	
67	## Traceability and repeatable cases
68	
69	QBrain records: `FR-GUESTADMIN-031`, `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043`,
70	`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149`; updated existing `FR-IDENTITY-018`,
71	`FR-PLAYERPROFILE-002`, `FR-ADMINPAGES-023`, `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026`,
72	`TR-IDENTITY-AUTHENTICATION-016`, `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036`,
73	`TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037`, `TEST-ADMINUI-136`, `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`,
74	`TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138` and `TEST-IDENTITYAUTHENTICATION-116`. Native mappings
75	preserve prior edges. Changed criteria remain unsatisfied until their new evidence
76	and independent review justify a separate status update.
77	
78	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-01/02` maps public guest-only behavior and disabled secured
79	  entry to identity/content/admin HTTP tests and the rendered navigation/content
80	  browser journeys. Original multi-account community UI cases are retained in
81	  `docs/testing/historical/*.spec.ts.txt`; inactive features are not silently
82	  represented as current successful UI coverage. Domain/transaction tests remain.
83	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-03/04/08` and `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043#GA-03/04/08` map to
84	  `TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` and `TEST-ADMINUI-136`. Provider fakes cover wrong numeric
85	  ID, wrong login, malformed state/PKCE, denied/token/network failures and claim
86	  minimization. Actual runtime/repository composition tests cover token namespace
87	  isolation, stripped guest grants and separate logout. HTTP tests cover cookies,
88	  malformed callback parameters, CSRF and private responses. Rendered pages test
89	  direct guest denial, safe callback feedback, logout, stale responses and retries.
90	- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-01..05` and `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036` map to
91	  `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`: inspect actual production HTML/manifest/icons; await real
92	  worker activation; inspect unfiltered Chromium installability diagnostics using
93	  a disposable regular profile; exercise click-only prompts and standalone hiding.
94	- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-06..09`, `TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037` and
95	  `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-05..07` map to `TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138`: inspect the actual
96	  static cache allowlist, abort the real worker's outgoing network request, require
97	  a fresh admin URL response from that worker, assert generic offline content and failed private/API/public
98	  requests, reconnect and require authentication again. Deterministic worker and
99	  client tests preserve unrelated registrations/caches during legacy retirement.
100	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-09` maps welcome/profile card whitespace to actual
101	 390px/1440px browser geometry and screenshots. Responsive padding is20px minimum
102	  on phones and32px on desktop, with no horizontal overflow.
103	
104	`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` objective is to prove that guest gameplay cannot grant
105	administration and that only the verified owner flow creates a usable admin
106	session. Priority is critical. Preconditions are an isolated database/network
107	adapter or declared HTTP fixture and independent guest/admin browser contexts.
108	Data includes owner numeric ID16146732, wrong ID16146733, wrong login, unique
109	opaque browser tokens, duplicate callback parameters and synthetic catalog cases.
110	Use phone390x844 and desktop1440x900, plus the existing enlargement/orientation
111	matrix. Never use live users or actual provider tokens as fixture data.
112	
113	Ordered actions and expected observations:
114	
115	1. Open public play, continue as guest, and attempt admin entry with only the
116	   guest credential. Guest play works; no public provider/install/delegation links
117	   appear; private APIs deny before reading records.
118	2. Complete a fixed-owner provider fixture, then try wrong ID/login, bad state,
119	   missing/expired/consumed challenge and malformed callbacks. Only the verified
120	   owner path may issue `wp_admin`; failures show safe feedback and no private UI.
121	3. Copy each issued opaque token into the other realm's cookie. Both copies fail.
122	   Sign out of admin with a same-origin request; only its stored session/cookie
123	   is revoked. A cross-origin request changes nothing.
124	4. Open admin word/hint forms, save/retry an uncertain write, and deny a mutation
125	   while an old read is pending. Existing versions/audit remain immutable, the
126	   command is reused without duplicates, and old responses cannot restore data.
127	5. Inspect installation metadata and activate the real admin worker; abort
128	   its outgoing network request and navigate to a fresh admin URL. Only a static reconnect screen appears.
129	   Reconnect and verify current authentication, never cached private content.
130	
131	Synchronization is condition-based: await responses, visible states, cache
132	contents and worker activation, without fixed sleeps. Cleanup closes owned
133	contexts/profiles and resets only disposable fixture resources. Automation is
134	ready through the named Vitest and Playwright suites; HTTP fixture evidence does
135	not establish live GitHub consent or phone OS installation.
136	
137	The offline browser case routes and aborts only service-worker-owned outgoing
138	network requests before enabling browser offline mode for subsequent API/public
139	checks. Chromium offline emulation alone intermittently left worker fetches online.
140	The case requires an actual worker response and records the intercepted request;
141	it never supplies mocked fallback HTML. This uses Playwright's documented
142	[service worker network routing](https://playwright.dev/docs/service-workers).
143	
144	```gherkin
145	Scenario: TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149 owner administration is isolated from guest play
146	  Given a browser has a valid guest session with stored administrator role data
147	  When it requests the administration session using only that guest token
148	  Then no administrator profile is returned
149	  And no private catalog records are read
150	  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146733 with login sharpninja
151	  Then the callback creates no administrator session
152	  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146732 with login sharpninja
153	  And its browser-bound challenge is current and unused
154	  Then only the administrator session cookie is issued
155	  And the existing guest session cookie is unchanged
156	  When the administrator signs out
157	  Then its stored administrator session is revoked
158	  And the guest session remains usable
159	```
160	
161	## Verification, operations and open dependencies
162	
163	Use `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, then production-browser
164	`npx playwright test --config=playwright.pwa.config.ts`. The full active browser
165	suite includes all currently enabled guest/game/admin flows. Source-level provider
166	and namespace tests are `tests/integration/github-admin.test.ts` and
167	`tests/integration/admin-session-isolation.test.ts`; HTTP checks include
168	`tests/web/github-admin-api.test.ts`. The hostile-review correction adds forward
169	migration `012_guest_public_profiles.sql`; no package is added. Existing schema
170	and private Realtime/scheduler remain separate deployment prerequisites.
171	
172	Real PostgreSQL coverage in `tests/integration/admin.integration.ts` exercises the
173	actual login/callback/session/content routes and runtime composition, with only
174	the external GitHub transport faked. It verifies stored one-time challenges,
175	cross-realm denial, catalog writes, callback replay and durable logout. Run the
176	full database suite with `tests/integration/run-phase1.ps1 -ReportDirectory <path>`;
177	`-VolatileStorage` uses an owned temporary PostgreSQL container and does not prove
178	disk durability or crash recovery. `scripts/Convert-JUnitToTrx.ps1` adapts each
179	native JUnit case into the review's TRX format, preserving original JUnit receipts.
180	TRX conversion timestamps are explicitly distinguished from execution times.
181	
182	The wider browser run also exposed a presence-timer regression:15-second profile
183	refreshes changed the profile object and restarted the20-second heartbeat effect.
184	Room refresh now depends on stable profile ID; the existing uncertain-readiness
185	browser case verifies repeated presence during a pending request. Artwork tests
186	now require absence of the removed public install panel and explicitly set their
187	desktop viewport instead of inheriting a phone viewport.
188	
189	Keep every failed test/build run and hostile-review round. Original admin ACL,
190	OpenAI and public-PWA receipts remain historical, not approval of these bytes.
191	The first architecture review rejected a nested manifest and missing callback
192	feedback; both findings require fresh final evidence. Final source review is
193	Claude Opus, explicitly selected by the operator. Real hosted GitHub consent,
194	standalone phone OAuth cookie continuity and physical OS installation remain
195	distinct from fixture/browser installability evidence. Deployment claims must
196	name the actual reviewed source commit and verified public endpoint.
197	
198	## Hostile-review recovery slice
199	
200	Claude Opus round1 rejected candidate437c501 at92%accuracy/88%completeness.
201	Its full findings and persistence proof are retained under `docs/receipts/hv/`.
202	The owner was created with the former member public-default, without a public
203	preferences route. The earlier PostgreSQL public-read failure exposed the extra
204	row; fixture cleanup made the suite independent but did not repair that product
205	privacy problem. That distinction was missing from the original failure analysis.
206	
207	The operator confirmed: "Hide all old member profiles". GA-10 therefore requires
208	new members to default private and all member identities, including retired
209	OpenAI records, to be excluded by the server's public query even if their stored
210	flag remains true. Preserve historical records, guest opt-in, ranking, paging and
211	revision conflicts. Add a forward SQL migration after the existing hosted history;
212	apply it to staging first, verify, then production. No data deletion or provider
213	token import is needed. Existing cached public pages may expire over their normal
214	five-minute read lifetime; restart/deployment creates fresh application caches.
215	
216	Before this correction, the independent GA-10 oracle accepted a private member
217	and guest-only rows, and rejected a public member and both owner/legacy leaks.
218	The mock gate passed3/3 at20:22:38 on28October2026. The same oracle is bound to
219	the real identity service and PostgreSQL query. This is evidence for the recovery
220	slice, not a reconstruction of the missing original pre-implementation gate.
221	The original slice's chronological process receipt remains missing and is not
222	claimed satisfied. On28October2026 the operator explicitly answered "Record the
223	one-time exception" to question `call_30e2a1f3011842979ab422d87f21432e`. This is a
224	one-time exception for that historical missing receipt only. It does not waive
225	fresh hostile validation, current tests, security checks, migration verification
226	or hosted observations. No original chronology is reconstructed. The decision
227	and QBrain readback are retained in `docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/process-exception.json`.
228	All current status/criteria remain in progress/unsatisfied.
229	
230	Recovery work also supplies explicit GA-05/06/07 cross-references to canonical
231	PWA criteria and their TEST/TR records, GA-09 on the responsive TR/admin TEST,
232	reproducible adapter fixtures and full post-edit PWA browser execution. No prior
233	failed review or test receipt is removed. Fresh review follows the full applicable
234	unit, PostgreSQL, browser, lint and production-build checks.
235	
236	Claude Opus round2 rejected the corrective candidate at95%accuracy and
237	94%completeness. Its four FAILs were a missing mock-first gate for the deployment
238	planner edit, continued extension of a Node script tool, an incomplete candidate
239	source hash manifest, and missing pre-run analyzer receipts for the JUnit/TRX
240	adapter scripts. The full verdict and request/response receipts remain under
241	`docs/receipts/hv/`. None of the four findings is represented as resolved by a
242	reviewer yet.
243	
244	For the next review, a PowerShell schema planner and CLI replace the Node planner.
245	The planner's six contract cases were written and run against correct and
246	intentionally wrong mocks before the PowerShell implementation. Their original
247	JUnit, mock-gate summary, real-run JUnit and adapted TRX receipts are in
248	`docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/planner-*`. The tracked source-manifest
249	generator enumerates literal Git paths, including bracketed routes, public assets
250	and root test/build configuration; its current path-set check covers276 files.
251	The adapter analyzer receipt records parser and ScriptAnalyzer results for both
252	scripts before the fresh three-fixture run. These are local process receipts, not
253	approval to deploy. The final source manifest and all execution reports must be
254	regenerated against the frozen source revision that the next hostile review sees.

updates wait for active clients and delete only older admin cache versions.

Public pages have no manifest or install controls. The former `/sw.js` remains
as a retirement worker with no fetch handler; it deletes only `wordpairs-pwa-*`
caches and unregisters itself. Root cleanup recognizes only that exact former
root registration and cache prefix, preserving admin and unrelated apps. Website
code cannot remove an existing OS home-screen icon or prevent browser bookmarks.

## Traceability and repeatable cases

QBrain records: `FR-GUESTADMIN-031`, `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043`,
`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149`; updated existing `FR-IDENTITY-018`,
`FR-PLAYERPROFILE-002`, `FR-ADMINPAGES-023`, `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026`,
`TR-IDENTITY-AUTHENTICATION-016`, `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036`,
`TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037`, `TEST-ADMINUI-136`, `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`,
`TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138` and `TEST-IDENTITYAUTHENTICATION-116`. Native mappings
preserve prior edges. Changed criteria remain unsatisfied until their new evidence
and independent review justify a separate status update.

- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-01/02` maps public guest-only behavior and disabled secured
  entry to identity/content/admin HTTP tests and the rendered navigation/content
  browser journeys. Original multi-account community UI cases are retained in
  `docs/testing/historical/*.spec.ts.txt`; inactive features are not silently
  represented as current successful UI coverage. Domain/transaction tests remain.
- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-03/04/08` and `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043#GA-03/04/08` map to
  `TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` and `TEST-ADMINUI-136`. Provider fakes cover wrong numeric
  ID, wrong login, malformed state/PKCE, denied/token/network failures and claim
  minimization. Actual runtime/repository composition tests cover token namespace
  isolation, stripped guest grants and separate logout. HTTP tests cover cookies,
  malformed callback parameters, CSRF and private responses. Rendered pages test
  direct guest denial, safe callback feedback, logout, stale responses and retries.
- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-01..05` and `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036` map to
  `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`: inspect actual production HTML/manifest/icons; await real
  worker activation; inspect unfiltered Chromium installability diagnostics using
  a disposable regular profile; exercise click-only prompts and standalone hiding.
- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-06..09`, `TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037` and
  `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-05..07` map to `TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138`: inspect the actual
  static cache allowlist, abort the real worker's outgoing network request, require
  a fresh admin URL response from that worker, assert generic offline content and failed private/API/public
  requests, reconnect and require authentication again. Deterministic worker and
  client tests preserve unrelated registrations/caches during legacy retirement.
- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-09` maps welcome/profile card whitespace to actual
 390px/1440px browser geometry and screenshots. Responsive padding is20px minimum
  on phones and32px on desktop, with no horizontal overflow.

`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` objective is to prove that guest gameplay cannot grant
administration and that only the verified owner flow creates a usable admin
session. Priority is critical. Preconditions are an isolated database/network
adapter or declared HTTP fixture and independent guest/admin browser contexts.
Data includes owner numeric ID16146732, wrong ID16146733, wrong login, unique
opaque browser tokens, duplicate callback parameters and synthetic catalog cases.
Use phone390x844 and desktop1440x900, plus the existing enlargement/orientation
matrix. Never use live users or actual provider tokens as fixture data.

Ordered actions and expected observations:

1. Open public play, continue as guest, and attempt admin entry with only the
   guest credential. Guest play works; no public provider/install/delegation links
   appear; private APIs deny before reading records.
2. Complete a fixed-owner provider fixture, then try wrong ID/login, bad state,
   missing/expired/consumed challenge and malformed callbacks. Only the verified
   owner path may issue `wp_admin`; failures show safe feedback and no private UI.
3. Copy each issued opaque token into the other realm's cookie. Both copies fail.
   Sign out of admin with a same-origin request; only its stored session/cookie
   is revoked. A cross-origin request changes nothing.
4. Open admin word/hint forms, save/retry an uncertain write, and deny a mutation
   while an old read is pending. Existing versions/audit remain immutable, the
   command is reused without duplicates, and old responses cannot restore data.
5. Inspect installation metadata and activate the real admin worker; abort
   its outgoing network request and navigate to a fresh admin URL. Only a static reconnect screen appears.
   Reconnect and verify current authentication, never cached private content.

Synchronization is condition-based: await responses, visible states, cache
contents and worker activation, without fixed sleeps. Cleanup closes owned
contexts/profiles and resets only disposable fixture resources. Automation is
ready through the named Vitest and Playwright suites; HTTP fixture evidence does
not establish live GitHub consent or phone OS installation.

The offline browser case routes and aborts only service-worker-owned outgoing
network requests before enabling browser offline mode for subsequent API/public
checks. Chromium offline emulation alone intermittently left worker fetches online.
The case requires an actual worker response and records the intercepted request;
it never supplies mocked fallback HTML. This uses Playwright's documented
[service worker network routing](https://playwright.dev/docs/service-workers).

```gherkin
Scenario: TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149 owner administration is isolated from guest play
  Given a browser has a valid guest session with stored administrator role data
  When it requests the administration session using only that guest token
  Then no administrator profile is returned
  And no private catalog records are read
  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146733 with login sharpninja
  Then the callback creates no administrator session
  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146732 with login sharpninja
  And its browser-bound challenge is current and unused
  Then only the administrator session cookie is issued
  And the existing guest session cookie is unchanged
  When the administrator signs out
  Then its stored administrator session is revoked
  And the guest session remains usable
```

## Verification, operations and open dependencies

Use `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, then production-browser
`npx playwright test --config=playwright.pwa.config.ts`. The full active browser
suite includes all currently enabled guest/game/admin flows. Source-level provider
and namespace tests are `tests/integration/github-admin.test.ts` and
`tests/integration/admin-session-isolation.test.ts`; HTTP checks include
`tests/web/github-admin-api.test.ts`. The hostile-review correction adds forward
migration `012_guest_public_profiles.sql`; no package is added. Existing schema
and private Realtime/scheduler remain separate deployment prerequisites.

Real PostgreSQL coverage in `tests/integration/admin.integration.ts` exercises the
actual login/callback/session/content routes and runtime composition, with only
the external GitHub transport faked. It verifies stored one-time challenges,
cross-realm denial, catalog writes, callback replay and durable logout. Run the
full database suite with `tests/integration/run-phase1.ps1 -ReportDirectory <path>`;
`-VolatileStorage` uses an owned temporary PostgreSQL container and does not prove
disk durability or crash recovery. `scripts/Convert-JUnitToTrx.ps1` adapts each
native JUnit case into the review's TRX format, preserving original JUnit receipts.
TRX conversion timestamps are explicitly distinguished from execution times.

The wider browser run also exposed a presence-timer regression:15-second profile
refreshes changed the profile object and restarted the20-second heartbeat effect.
Room refresh now depends on stable profile ID; the existing uncertain-readiness
browser case verifies repeated presence during a pending request. Artwork tests
now require absence of the removed public install panel and explicitly set their
desktop viewport instead of inheriting a phone viewport.

Keep every failed test/build run and hostile-review round. Original admin ACL,
OpenAI and public-PWA receipts remain historical, not approval of these bytes.
The first architecture review rejected a nested manifest and missing callback
feedback; both findings require fresh final evidence. Final source review is
Claude Opus, explicitly selected by the operator. Real hosted GitHub consent,
standalone phone OAuth cookie continuity and physical OS installation remain
distinct from fixture/browser installability evidence. Deployment claims must
name the actual reviewed source commit and verified public endpoint.

## Hostile-review recovery slice

Claude Opus round1 rejected candidate437c501 at92%accuracy/88%completeness.
Its full findings and persistence proof are retained under `docs/receipts/hv/`.
The owner was created with the former member public-default, without a public
preferences route. The earlier PostgreSQL public-read failure exposed the extra
row; fixture cleanup made the suite independent but did not repair that product
privacy problem. That distinction was missing from the original failure analysis.

The operator confirmed: "Hide all old member profiles". GA-10 therefore requires
new members to default private and all member identities, including retired
OpenAI records, to be excluded by the server's public query even if their stored
flag remains true. Preserve historical records, guest opt-in, ranking, paging and
revision conflicts. Add a forward SQL migration after the existing hosted history;
apply it to staging first, verify, then production. No data deletion or provider
token import is needed. Existing cached public pages may expire over their normal
five-minute read lifetime; restart/deployment creates fresh application caches.

Before this correction, the independent GA-10 oracle accepted a private member
and guest-only rows, and rejected a public member and both owner/legacy leaks.
The mock gate passed3/3 at20:22:38 on28October2026. The same oracle is bound to
the real identity service and PostgreSQL query. This is evidence for the recovery
slice, not a reconstruction of the missing original pre-implementation gate.
The original slice's chronological process receipt remains missing and is not
claimed satisfied. On28October2026 the operator explicitly answered "Record the
one-time exception" to question `call_30e2a1f3011842979ab422d87f21432e`. This is a
one-time exception for that historical missing receipt only. It does not waive
fresh hostile validation, current tests, security checks, migration verification
or hosted observations. No original chronology is reconstructed. The decision
and QBrain readback are retained in `docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/process-exception.json`.
All current status/criteria remain in progress/unsatisfied.

Recovery work also supplies explicit GA-05/06/07 cross-references to canonical
PWA criteria and their TEST/TR records, GA-09 on the responsive TR/admin TEST,
reproducible adapter fixtures and full post-edit PWA browser execution. No prior
failed review or test receipt is removed. Fresh review follows the full applicable
unit, PostgreSQL, browser, lint and production-build checks.

Claude Opus round2 rejected the corrective candidate at95%accuracy and
94%completeness. Its four FAILs were a missing mock-first gate for the deployment
planner edit, continued extension of a Node script tool, an incomplete candidate
source hash manifest, and missing pre-run analyzer receipts for the JUnit/TRX
adapter scripts. The full verdict and request/response receipts remain under
`docs/receipts/hv/`. None of the four findings is represented as resolved by a
reviewer yet.

For the next review, a PowerShell schema planner and CLI replace the Node planner.
The planner's six contract cases were written and run against correct and
intentionally wrong mocks before the PowerShell implementation. Their original
JUnit, mock-gate summary, real-run JUnit and adapted TRX receipts are in
`docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/planner-*`. The tracked source-manifest
generator enumerates literal Git paths, including bracketed routes, public assets
and root test/build configuration; its current path-set check covers276 files.
The adapter analyzer receipt records parser and ScriptAnalyzer results for both
scripts before the fresh three-fixture run. These are local process receipts, not
approval to deploy. The final source manifest and all execution reports must be
regenerated against the frozen source revision that the next hostile review sees.

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$ReportDirectory)
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
$root=(Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../..')).ProviderPath
$test=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.Tests.ps1'
$correct=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockCorrect.psm1'
$wrong=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockWrong.psm1'
if(-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($ReportDirectory,'Run independent planner mock gate and save evidence')){return}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ReportDirectory -Force|Out-Null
$runs=@()
foreach($case in @(@{name='correct';module=$correct},@{name='wrong';module=$wrong})){
    $env:WORDPAIRS_PLANNER_MODULE=$case.module
    $configuration=New-PesterConfiguration
    $configuration.Run.Path=@($test)
    $configuration.Run.PassThru=$true
    $configuration.Output.Verbosity='Detailed'
    $configuration.TestResult.Enabled=$true
    $configuration.TestResult.OutputFormat='NUnitXml'
    $configuration.TestResult.OutputPath=Join-Path $ReportDirectory ($case.name+'.xml')
    $result=Invoke-Pester -Configuration $configuration
    $runs+= [pscustomobject]@{name=$case.name;passed=$result.PassedCount;failed=$result.FailedCount;skipped=$result.SkippedCount}
}
Remove-Item Env:WORDPAIRS_PLANNER_MODULE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if($runs[0].passed -ne 6 -or $runs[0].failed -ne 0 -or $runs[0].skipped -ne 0 -or $runs[1].failed -lt 3){throw 'Mock gate did not discriminate expected behavior.'}
$receipt=[pscustomobject]@{
    timestamp=Get-Date -Format s
    root=$root
    test=(Resolve-Path $test).ProviderPath
    testSha256=(Get-FileHash $test -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    correctMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $correct -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    wrongMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $wrong -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    runs=$runs
    qualification='The same Pester scenarios will be rebound to the PowerShell production planner after this mock gate.'
}
$receipt|ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6|Set-Content (Join-Path $ReportDirectory 'mock-gate.json')
$receipt|ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6

#Requires -Version 7.0
# Round3 retry review tool A10: read-only parser plus PSScriptAnalyzer (Warning, Error) over product PowerShell
# scripts named by a comma-separated workspace-relative list. Static analysis only; nothing is executed or edited.
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$PathList
)
Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$ws = '[HOME]/github/WordGame/.mcpServer/wordpairs'
Write-Output ("ANALYZE-PRODUCT-TIME: {0}" -f (Get-Date -Format s))
$module = Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name PSScriptAnalyzer | Sort-Object Version -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
Write-Output ("PSScriptAnalyzer: {0}" -f $(if ($module) { $module.Version } else { 'NOT AVAILABLE' }))
foreach ($rel in @($PathList -split ',' | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ })) {
    $abs = Join-Path $ws $rel

5	$plugin = '[HOME]/github/mcpserver-claude-code-plugin'

11	$jsonText = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($verdictPath)
12	$verdict = $jsonText | ConvertFrom-Json -DateKind String
13	$utcNow = { (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ') }
14	
15	function Invoke-Plugin([string]$Method, $Params) {
16	    $result = & $wrapper -Command Invoke -Method $Method -ParamsObject $Params -WorkspacePath $ws -PluginRoot $plugin 2>&1
17	    $text = ($result | ForEach-Object { [string]$_ }) -join "`n"
18	    $code = [regex]::Match($text, '(?m)^\s*code:\s*(\S+)').Groups[1].Value
19	    $persisted = [regex]::Match($text, '(?m)^\s*persisted:\s*(\S+)').Groups[1].Value

23	}

27	for ($i = 0; $i -lt $jsonText.Length; $i += $chunkSize) { $chunks.Add($jsonText.Substring($i, [Math]::Min($chunkSize, $jsonText.Length - $i))) }

   description: Players can browse discoverable open lobbies or use quick match to join an available lobby for this game. Any player in a room can share its room code or deep link to invite others; a deep link bypasses lobby browsing. Joining as a player requires an available slot under the configured capacity. An invited player who reaches a full room can choose observer mode. Before the game start countdown begins, if a player leaves a full room, the oldest observer is promoted into the final player position and the remaining players move up to close the vacancy. If player/observer membership or readiness has not changed for 30 seconds before countdown, all players are prompted once for that room version to mark ready; any such change resets the interval. When all but one player have marked ready, the holdout receives a five-second warning. If they mark ready before it expires, the countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires while the holdout remains unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the countdown begins. In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins, and a player who leaves afterward is not replaced. Rooms are private by default; the creator may enable discoverability. Quick match selects the oldest eligible room, breaking equal creation times by stable room ID. These joins use the same atomic capacity check.

59	   description: Players can browse discoverable open lobbies or use quick match to join an available lobby for this game. Any player in a room can share its room code or deep link to invite others; a deep link bypasses lobby browsing. Joining as a player requires an available slot under the configured capacity. An invited player who reaches a full room can choose observer mode. Before the game start countdown begins, if a player leaves a full room, the oldest observer is promoted into the final player position and the remaining players move up to close the vacancy. If player/observer membership or readiness has not changed for 30 seconds before countdown, all players are prompted once for that room version to mark ready; any such change resets the interval. When all but one player have marked ready, the holdout receives a five-second warning. If they mark ready before it expires, the countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires while the holdout remains unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the countdown begins. In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins, and a player who leaves afterward is not replaced. Rooms are private by default; the creator may enable discoverability. Quick match selects the oldest eligible room, breaking equal creation times by stable room ID. These joins use the same atomic capacity check.

An invited player who reaches a full room can choose observer mode. Before the game start countdown begins, if a player leaves a full room, the oldest observer is promoted into the final player position and the remaining players move up to close the vacancy. If the warning expires while the holdout remains unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the countdown begins. In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins, and a player who leaves afterward is not replaced. Rooms are private by default; the creator may enable discoverability. 1	# Wordpairs Implementation Plan
2	
3	Current release override, 28 October 2026: [guest game and GitHub admin PWA](admin_pwa_release.md)
4	defines the authorized guest-only public surface and fixed-owner GitHub admin PWA.
5	Earlier public OpenAI, community submission, delegation and public installation
6	portions below are historical. The current slice requires unit, PostgreSQL and
7	rendered-browser evidence, Claude Opus hostile validation, then deployment of the
8	exact reviewed commit to staging before production. Physical phone installation
9	and hosted OAuth continuity remain separate observations and are never inferred
10	from browser fixtures.
11	
12	**Status:** Coding Phases 0–6 complete and independently approved; administration/ACL extension reviewed; Phase 7 deployment remains future work
13	**Planning baseline:** Requirements v2.6, 26 October 2026
14	**Process:** Byrd Development Process draft v4  
15	**Target repository:** `sharpninja/wordpairs`  
16	**Execution tracker:** [`implementation_phase0_execution.md`](implementation_phase0_execution.md)
17	
18	Current execution evidence is in [`phase6_execution.md`](phase6_execution.md), with subsequent administration behavior and validation in [`admin_acl_design.md`](admin_acl_design.md) and [`admin_acl_review_receipt.json`](admin_acl_review_receipt.json). The ordered gates below describe the completed coding sequence and the remaining deployment contract. They do not reopen completed phase approvals or impose a personal human sign-off gate.
19	
20	The subsequent [phone PWA extension](pwa_design.md) adds home-screen installation, standalone launch and a private-data-safe offline reconnect screen. It is tracked separately from historical coding-phase approvals and does not claim a hosted release or physical-phone installation from browser emulation.
21	
22	## 1. Purpose and governing documents
23	
24	This plan decomposes the current requirements into reviewable coding increments, each with explicit acceptance-criterion coverage and a mock-first test gate. Deployment and release operations are a separate post-coding phase. The functional and technical requirements and acceptance criteria in [`word_association_game_requirements.md`](word_association_game_requirements.md) remain authoritative. This plan does not silently weaken any acceptance criterion.
25	
26	Deployment, provisioning, SWBOM generation, environment isolation, and deployment-build gates are TR-bound technical work, not AC-bound behaviors. Their mockable checks are test-first, while live deployment/account checks remain technical integration/operational evidence and cannot satisfy AC coverage.
27	
28	The work follows the [Byrd Development Process v4](https://github.com/sharpninja/McpServer/blob/main/docs/Development-Process-draft-v4.md), with the stricter project-specific gate explicitly required by the user: complete planning and define iterations before implementation; discover components and document public interfaces before code; after Phase 0 approval, author the full executable test suite for all active ACs, validate every test against mocks, and only then begin any production implementation code. After that global gate, implement Phases 1–6 in small coding increments, keep the full prior suite green, add integration tests after unit tests are established, and validate with human users where appropriate. Begin deployment and release operations only after coding is complete. Deployed artifacts and deployment/account checks are never AC evidence.
29	
30	### Non-negotiable implementation rules
31	
32	1. **No tests or implementation code before Phase 0 approval.** Phase 0 exit requires a final expected outcome and evidence disposition for every active AC. Resolve every decision that changes an active AC's expected result; if behavior is deferred, formally revise the requirements so the AC is not in the active baseline. A blocked, expectation-free test cannot pass Phase 0.
33	2. **100% acceptance-criterion traceability.** Every active AC has at least one named test case before its behavior is implemented. No AC is counted as covered merely because a nearby scenario happens to exercise it.
34	3. **Global mock-oracle gate before project implementation.** After Phase 0 is approved and expected behavior is fixed, bootstrap only the reviewed test toolchain/configuration (no product behavior), then author all active-AC contract oracles. For each oracle, validate that a conforming scripted mock trace is accepted and a deliberately violating trace is rejected before writing production implementation code. This proves the test assertions are sensitive; it does not prove the application behavior. Keep the same oracles and run them against each real implementation increment. Database concurrency, RLS, transactional durability, deployment, and other system-level integration tests are additional evidence tiers: define their contract assertions before implementation, validate the application/domain contracts with mocks, then run the separate real-system tests against disposable environments after adapters exist. These integration checks are TR/operational evidence only and never count toward AC coverage. A mock does not prove a database invariant or external platform fact.
