150	## 5. Global mock-validation gate and incremental TDD protocol
151	
152	Phase 0 is approved. Before any production implementation code, author and mock-validate the complete contract-test suite for every active AC. Mockable TR contracts are validated before their respective implementation; deployment TR tooling is implemented only in post-coding Phase 7. Live deployment/account/database checks are TR-only integration or operational evidence and do not count as AC coverage. Once the global mock-validation gate passes, apply this sequence to each small coding increment:
153	
154	1. **Select scope:** identify the approved requirement and AC IDs; state the behavior, invariant, and exclusions. Confirm no unresolved decision changes expected results.
155	2. **Design boundary:** identify the public interface and injected collaborators. For time, randomness, network, persistence, identity, and event delivery, define deterministic seams before test authoring.
156	3. **Write the AC-to-test mapping:** record at least one test case for each applicable AC and each important boundary case. Include negative/security cases and concurrent state changes when relevant.
157	4. **Build mocks/fakes:** provide executable mock adapters that represent the specified public contract. Keep assertions on observable behavior; do not let the mock implement the business rule being tested.
158	5. **Global pre-implementation mock-oracle validation:** before production code, execute all 67 AC oracles against conforming and violating scripted mock traces; every oracle must accept the conforming trace and reject its targeted mutation. This validates assertion sensitivity only. Record every test ID, command, result, and evidence boundary. Then run the same oracles against each real implementation increment and record product-conformance separately.
159	6. **TR-19 reaction-policy contracts:** keep `TR-19-T01` through `TR-19-T04` separate from AC coverage. Before reaction implementation, validate the complete emoji allowlist, exact five-second visibility, one-per-player-per-two-second rate rule, full player/observer audience, and game-state invariance against conforming and violating mock observations.
160	7. **Implement the smallest behavior:** after the global gate passes, use failing contracts as targets within a small increment. Avoid unrelated refactoring or scope additions.
161	8. **Run increment and regression suites:** run all tests for this increment plus all previous increments. Keep production integration separate from the mock contract tests.
162	9. **Integrate real adapters:** after unit tests pass, add integration tests against disposable/local services; only use test credentials and seeded data. Do not replace mock-first unit tests with integration-only coverage.
163	10. **Review evidence:** verify AC mapping, test output, security boundaries, accessibility, docs, migrations, and artifact effects. Update the matrix whenever requirements change.
164	11. **Close increment:** merge only when checks pass and the work is reviewable. Validate the branch locally and against disposable services. Vercel Preview deployment and its SWBOM occur only in Phase 7, after coding Phases 1–6 are complete. Record agent visual/usability review and any optional human feedback separately; a mandatory personal sign-off applies only if explicitly requested by the user.

181	## 7. Architecture and implementation order
182	
183	### 7.1 Trust and authority
184	
185	The browser is an untrusted presentation/client. A server-side application service owns membership, roster order, readiness, countdown transitions, answer validation, hint visibility, scoring, timestamps, category permissions, nomination eligibility, moderation state, and final ranking. Database constraints and transactions backstop service checks. Clients cannot choose trusted identity claims, promote themselves, assign points, reveal targets, alter the roster after lock, or mutate state through observer sessions.
186	
187	Use a server-owned clock and injected random source. Assign a stable event/order key to simultaneous submissions and membership events. Persist the authoritative transition before broadcasting it. Realtime delivery is a view of committed state, not the source of truth. Define idempotency keys for joins, guesses, reactions, and moderation actions so retries do not duplicate side effects.
188	
189	### 7.2 Suggested module boundaries
190	
191	- `domain/`: typed entities, value objects, validation, state machines, scoring, and pure policies.
192	- `application/`: use cases and transaction orchestration; depends on interfaces only.
193	- `adapters/supabase/`: queries, migrations, transaction/RPC functions, row-level security, and Realtime transport.
194	- `adapters/identity/`: OIDC token verification and guest session issuance.
195	- `web/`: Next.js routes, server actions/API handlers, accessible React views, and client event subscriptions.
196	- `content/`: curated seed records and category backgrounds; validation runs at build and import.
197	- `tests/`: unit, component, service-contract, integration, and browser suites organized by AC ID.
198	- `scripts/`: provisioning, migration/status checks, SWBOM validation, release archive creation, and archive inspection. Scripts are safe to rerun and redact secrets.
199	
200	This section preserves the original planning boundary map. The implemented layout uses `src/domain`, `src/application`, `src/infrastructure`, `src/web` and App Router entries under `src/app`; see [local development](local_development.md). Provisioning and operational release scripts in this planned map remain Phase 7 work.
201	
202	### 7.3 Critical data invariants
203	
204	- Active player count never exceeds room capacity (2–25); assignment is atomic under concurrency.
205	- A player appears once in an active roster; order is explicit and stable except the confirmed pre-countdown compaction rule.
206	- Promotion only occurs before countdown start, selects the earliest observer, places them last, shifts other players up without reordering them, and preserves remaining observers.
207	- Start countdown and roster lock happen atomically when all players are ready, or when an expired holdout is removed from a room with more than two players. In an exactly two-player room, expiry leaves the holdout in place and does not start the countdown. After lock, departures create a vacancy and never trigger replacement.
208	- A 30-second idle readiness prompt and 5-second holdout warning are driven from authoritative state/version timestamps, so stale timer callbacks cannot mutate a changed lobby.
209	- One accepted score per player per round; stage score is fixed at acceptance. Hints go only to players unsolved at the current transition.
210	- The target answer is never sent before reveal; incorrect guess text is never broadcast to other players or observers.
211	- Observer identity is bound to approved invite context; observer commands are read-only and scoreless.
212	- The landing page uses a public read-only projection with an allowlist of approved leaderboard/lobby fields; it cannot query private room state or mutate game state.
213	- OIDC authentication creates an authenticated profile only after server validation of the configured provider's signature and required claims.
214	- Moderation and catalog activation are separately authorized; candidate approval never directly makes incomplete content playable.
215	- Provisioning separates Preview/Staging and Production targets and can be safely repeated without exposing secrets or erasing user data.
216	- Domain policies are pure and framework-independent; each room mutation uses a transactional lock/version check, idempotency key, and same-transaction outbox event.
217	- Only approved, complete content records are playable; nominations/suggestions cannot bypass moderation or catalog validation.
218	
219	## 8. Post-coding deployment, release, licensing, and SWBOM
220	
221	This section applies only after coding Phases 1–6 are complete. Deployment is not part of those coding phases.
222	
223	Vercel Git integration creates Preview deployments for non-production branches and Production deployments from `main`. Configure a persistent Staging Preview path plus Development and Production credentials. The app build command first runs the complete test suite. After tests pass, generate a CycloneDX JSON 1.6 SWBOM from the exact committed lockfile and Vercel build metadata, then build the app so the report is included at `public/sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json` in that immutable deployment. The report includes direct/transitive runtime and development components, declared licenses, package URLs, dependency relationships, build timestamp, commit SHA, deployment environment, and deployment URL; it contains no secrets.
224	
225	For each release, a manual, reproducible packaging command obtains the SWBOM for the selected Production deployment and verifies schema, hash/commit identity, and required metadata. It creates a source archive containing the complete source for that release, root `LICENSE`, attribution notices, and the same report at `sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json`. Validate the archive contents and open/read the SWBOM before publishing the release. Fail closed if the report is missing, invalid, secret-bearing, or references a different commit. Do not substitute a newly generated report from a different dependency lockfile or a Preview deployment.
226	
227	Before locking dependencies, review direct/transitive licenses and whether shipped browser bundles/assets constitute redistributed components. Planned Apache-2.0 developer/build tools must remain tooling-only; preserve their notices as required by their terms and do not bundle them as game runtime code. A SWBOM's declared license field is an inventory, not an automatic compatibility ruling. The attribution document must track all direct dependencies and externally sourced assets; refresh it and the SWBOM whenever dependency or asset inputs change.
228	
229	## 9. Project risks and controls
230	
231	| Risk | Control / proof required |
232	|---|---|
233	| Ambiguous rules cause rework or incompatible tests. | Resolve decisions before affected AC tests; update approved requirements and traceability first. |
234	| Timer/event races corrupt room state. | State-versioned deadlines, server clock, transactional transitions, deterministic race tests, idempotency. |
235	| Concurrent joins overfill rooms. | Atomic database reservation and concurrency integration tests; quick-match uses the same reservation path as direct join. |
236	| OIDC assumptions fail against the chosen provider. | Verify discovery metadata and token-validation contract in planning; mock success/failure first; no token trust from browser input. |
237	| Realtime exposes hidden answers or private guesses. | Explicit event allowlist and per-recipient projections; security tests assert secret fields are absent. |
238	| Free-tier pause/quota disrupts play. | Isolated quota adapter, recoverable UX, validate the fixed v2.6 target of one full 25-player room plus up to 25 observers during Phase 7 quota simulation; no paid fallback. |
239	| GPL conflict in runtime/transitive bundle or artwork. | Lockfile/SWBOM/license review before adding or shipping each component; preserve notices; release gate blocks unresolved licenses. |
240	| Mock differs from Supabase/OIDC behavior. | Adapter contract tests plus staged integration test suite after mock-first unit tests. |
241	| Build artifact and source archive describe different commits. | Embed commit SHA in SWBOM; verify deployment, source tag, lockfile, and archive all match before publication. |
242	| Context/process drift skips a gate. | Keep this plan, AC traceability, and per-increment evidence in the repo; each work item names AC IDs and mock-first gate. |
243	
244	## 10. Completion definition
245	
246	A coding increment is complete only when its approved ACs map to passing mock-first tests, implementation and regression suites pass, security/data invariants are verified, and migrations/interfaces are documented. Do not deploy during coding Phases 1–6. After those phases and the full active-AC suite complete, Phase 7 performs deployment, operational verification, and release packaging. Deployment checks and deployed artifacts remain outside AC coverage.
247	
248	The global AC mock-oracle suite had 67 primary AC scenarios, 27 supplemental scenarios, four separate TR-19 cases and 112 named controls; its 316 tests passed independent exact-commit review at 99% accuracy / 100% completeness on `f7b5ff8302e24c6eae4dd1d2f21d7cba8577ac29`. Phases 1–6 subsequently implemented and independently validated the application, including gameplay. [Phase 6](phase6_execution.md) records formal coding completion. The later administration extension passed 502 unit/contract tests, 66 PostgreSQL tests, 31 browser journeys and the production build, with an independent 99/99 review. Those extension results supplement the historical baseline; they do not replace its recorded source-bound acceptance mapping or claim Phase 7 completion.
249	
250	## Live transport follow-up
251	
252	The phone stale-roster defect expanded the follow-up from lobby recovery to actual private delivery and autonomous progression. [The reviewed plan and execution evidence](room_sync_fix.md) cover real UI integration, scheduler failure handling, bounded publication, resume coalescing and lifecycle cleanup. The previous administration/PWA review receipts remain historical snapshots.
253

# Wordpairs Implementation Plan

Current release override, 28 October 2026: [guest game and GitHub admin PWA](admin_pwa_release.md)
defines the authorized guest-only public surface and fixed-owner GitHub admin PWA.
Earlier public OpenAI, community submission, delegation and public installation
portions below are historical. The current slice requires unit, PostgreSQL and
rendered-browser evidence, Claude Opus hostile validation, then deployment of the
exact reviewed commit to staging before production. Physical phone installation
and hosted OAuth continuity remain separate observations and are never inferred
from browser fixtures.

**Status:** Coding Phases 0–6 complete and independently approved; administration/ACL extension reviewed; Phase 7 deployment remains future work
**Planning baseline:** Requirements v2.6, 26 October 2026
**Process:** Byrd Development Process draft v4  
**Target repository:** `sharpninja/wordpairs`  
**Execution tracker:** [`implementation_phase0_execution.md`](implementation_phase0_execution.md)

Current execution evidence is in [`phase6_execution.md`](phase6_execution.md), with subsequent administration behavior and validation in [`admin_acl_design.md`](admin_acl_design.md) and [`admin_acl_review_receipt.json`](admin_acl_review_receipt.json). The ordered gates below describe the completed coding sequence and the remaining deployment contract. They do not reopen completed phase approvals or impose a personal human sign-off gate.

The subsequent [phone PWA extension](pwa_design.md) adds home-screen installation, standalone launch and a private-data-safe offline reconnect screen. It is tracked separately from historical coding-phase approvals and does not claim a hosted release or physical-phone installation from browser emulation.

## 1. Purpose and governing documents

This plan decomposes the current requirements into reviewable coding increments, each with explicit acceptance-criterion coverage and a mock-first test gate. Deployment and release operations are a separate post-coding phase. The functional and technical requirements and acceptance criteria in [`word_association_game_requirements.md`](word_association_game_requirements.md) remain authoritative. This plan does not silently weaken any acceptance criterion.

Deployment, provisioning, SWBOM generation, environment isolation, and deployment-build gates are TR-bound technical work, not AC-bound behaviors. Their mockable checks are test-first, while live deployment/account checks remain technical integration/operational evidence and cannot satisfy AC coverage.

The work follows the [Byrd Development Process v4](https://github.com/sharpninja/McpServer/blob/main/docs/Development-Process-draft-v4.md), with the stricter project-specific gate explicitly required by the user: complete planning and define iterations before implementation; discover components and document public interfaces before code; after Phase 0 approval, author the full executable test suite for all active ACs, validate every test against mocks, and only then begin any production implementation code. After that global gate, implement Phases 1–6 in small coding increments, keep the full prior suite green, add integration tests after unit tests are established, and validate with human users where appropriate. Begin deployment and release operations only after coding is complete. Deployed artifacts and deployment/account checks are never AC evidence.

### Non-negotiable implementation rules

1. **No tests or implementation code before Phase 0 approval.** Phase 0 exit requires a final expected outcome and evidence disposition for every active AC. Resolve every decision that changes an active AC's expected result; if behavior is deferred, formally revise the requirements so the AC is not in the active baseline. A blocked, expectation-free test cannot pass Phase 0.
2. **100% acceptance-criterion traceability.** Every active AC has at least one named test case before its behavior is implemented. No AC is counted as covered merely because a nearby scenario happens to exercise it.
3. **Global mock-oracle gate before project implementation.** After Phase 0 is approved and expected behavior is fixed, bootstrap only the reviewed test toolchain/configuration (no product behavior), then author all active-AC contract oracles. For each oracle, validate that a conforming scripted mock trace is accepted and a deliberately violating trace is rejected before writing production implementation code. This proves the test assertions are sensitive; it does not prove the application behavior. Keep the same oracles and run them against each real implementation increment. Database concurrency, RLS, transactional durability, deployment, and other system-level integration tests are additional evidence tiers: define their contract assertions before implementation, validate the application/domain contracts with mocks, then run the separate real-system tests against disposable environments after adapters exist. These integration checks are TR/operational evidence only and never count toward AC coverage. A mock does not prove a database invariant or external platform fact. Do not replace a failing test, relax an assertion, or label a valid test invalid to make progress.
4. **Green regression suite at every increment boundary.** Run all tests for the current increment and all earlier increments before marking the increment complete.
5. **No GitHub Actions dependency.** Use Vercel Git integration for branch previews and production. Run provisioning and release packaging manually from an authenticated workstation, as specified in the requirements.
6. **Free-tier boundary.** Use Vercel Hobby and Supabase Free only. Do not silently enable paid services, usage, add-ons, or upgrades.
7. **GPL and supply-chain records.** Keep project source under GPL-2.0-only; review every distributed dependency and asset for compatibility and notices. Generate a commit-specific CycloneDX SWBOM for each Preview and Production deployment and include the matching SWBOM plus `LICENSE` in each release archive; deployment behavior is TR-bound, while source-archive contents remain independently fixture-testable under AC-41/42.

### Validation responsibility clarification

The user's execution goal requires independent hostile validation by GPT-6 Astra/high at each coding-phase exit. On 26 October 2026 the user corrected the personal-sign-off interpretation: "I don't recall adding human review gates". The plan's human-validation method wording was not a separately requested mandatory user sign-off. Automated acceptance and independent agent visual/usability review establish the coding-phase UX evidence; human feedback is optional unless the user explicitly requests a human gate. This corrects an agent-added blocker. It does not claim that human testing occurred or that the user waived an explicitly requested gate. Product ACs, test assertions, review thresholds and the Phase 7 deployment boundary remain unchanged.

## 2. Approved Phase 0 baseline: architecture and interfaces

Requirements v2.6 resolves product decisions that affect active AC expected results. Phase 0 was approved by the user on 26 October 2026 after technical review of the selected architecture and contracts and hostile validation of the baseline. If a later change affects an AC expected result, revise the baseline and test specification before implementation.

| Technical artifact | Phase 0 disposition | Primary impact |
|---|---|---|
| Stack and architecture ADR | Selected baseline: Next.js/TypeScript/npm; Vitest, MSW/fakes, Testing Library, Playwright; modular monolith with DDD boundaries and ports/adapters. The selected architecture is approved; install the recorded compatible versions as test tooling. | Test setup, module boundaries and toolchain (AC-38/39; TR-26–29). |
| Public application interfaces | Review command/query inputs, result/error types, authorization, event schemas, projection allowlists, idempotency keys and clock ownership in the Phase 0 contract draft. | Every active AC and server boundary. |
| Data/security contract | Approve logical schema, RLS, transaction/version strategy, moderator role source, secret handling, no raw incorrect-guess persistence, retention, idempotency and outbox lifecycle. | AC-28/37/45/47/50/51; TR-01–05/09/22/23/31. |
| Deadline behavior | v2.6 selects 20-second answer stages, 30-second lobby-idle prompt, five-second holdout warning, 10-second countdown, versioned deadlines, and Supabase Cron/pg_cron adapter. Verify Free-plan operational availability only in post-coding Phase 7. | AC-30–33; TR-22. |
| Content and privacy contract | v2.6 sets 10 initial pairs per category, no within-match repeat before pool exhaustion, unique-player nomination count, moderation roles/appeal, generated aliases, public leaderboard and lobby allowlists. | AC-05/16–19/43/47/50. |
| Deployment and release contracts | Vercel/Supabase/Hobby/Free/manual workflow and SWBOM/archive contracts remain TR-only. Specify them during planning, but implement/configure/deploy only after coding Phases 1–6 in Phase 7. | TR-20–29; AC-41/42 cover temporary source-archive fixtures only. |

The following design artifacts were reviewed and approved at Phase 0 exit:

- Architecture decision record recording the selected Next.js/TypeScript/npm stack and detailing Vercel/Supabase adapters, guest/OpenAI OIDC identity, and server-authoritative game state. Vercel and Supabase are requirements (TR-20–TR-24); the v2.6 baseline selects the framework and language.
- Pattern decision record in [`architecture_patterns.md`](architecture_patterns.md) covering DDD boundaries, ports/adapters, pure policy testing, room transactions, idempotency, and transactional outbox.
- Context/container diagram and trust-boundary notes. Identify browser, Next.js server/API, Supabase database, Realtime, identity provider, Vercel deployment, and operator workstation responsibilities.
- Domain model and state-transition diagrams for room/lobby readiness, membership/observer promotion, match, round/hint stages, nominations, moderation, and suggestions.
- Public interface specifications: route/action inputs and outputs, event names/payloads, authorization checks, error codes, and versioning policy. Document which side owns each timer and timestamp.
- Database schema and migrations for profiles, rooms, ordered player roster, observers/invitation context, ready states, curated categories/pairs, matches/rounds/submissions/scores, nominations, moderation, suggestions, and audit events. Include uniqueness, foreign-key, transaction, retention, and row-level-security policies.
- Mock boundary catalog: clock, random-number source, repository/database, Realtime publisher/subscriber, OIDC verifier, environment/quota status, and Vercel build metadata. Production logic must depend on these interfaces rather than hidden globals.
- Requirements-to-test traceability matrix, initial content plan, accessibility checks, security/threat review, deployment constraints and abstract environment-isolation evidence, and release/SWBOM artifact contract. Final branch/project topology and account-capacity verification are post-coding Phase 7 deployment-entry decisions, not Phase 0 exit conditions.
- The approved command, event, logical data, authorization, transaction, and timer contracts are in [`phase0_interface_and_data_contracts.md`](phase0_interface_and_data_contracts.md).

## 3. Delivery sequence and phase gates

Phases are ordered by dependency. Phase 0 was the planning-only gate and has passed. No production implementation code may be authored until the global active-AC mock-validation gate passes. After Phase 0, all active AC tests must be authored and mock-validated as a single global pre-implementation gate; only then may project implementation begin. Implementation may then proceed in small increments, with each increment's applicable tests run and the complete existing regression suite green. External account, static configuration, integration, deployment, and human evidence may be required by TRs or operational release policy, but no AC depends on deployed artifacts and none of that evidence contributes to AC coverage.

| Phase | Outcome and included work | AC coverage | Entry and exit gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0 — Planning closure** | Approve the v2.6 product baseline, selected architecture, interfaces, database/security contract, content seed approach, AC traceability, dependency/license review, test strategy, and iteration order. Specify all test expectations without authoring executable tests. | Every active criterion has a fixed expected result, test IDs, and evidence tiers. | Exit after baseline and technical contract approval, complete active-AC traceability, and hostile validation. No executable tests, project scripts/configuration, or production code. |
| **1 — Core application foundation** | After the global mock gate, create the application skeleton, lock direct dependencies, establish test scripts, implement core ports/adapters for persistence and identity, define migrations/schema, quota handling, and modular import boundaries. Do not configure or deploy Vercel environments in this coding phase. | Active AC-37, AC-39, AC-51; application persistence contracts TR-22–TR-23. | Keep unit/use-case suites green; mock-validate each TR contract before its implementation. Database integration evidence uses local/disposable services. |
| **2 — Public landing, identity, profiles, room creation and joining** | Implement the anonymous landing page with the approved leaderboard projection, public discoverable-lobby summary, and gameplay rules; then guest and approved OIDC profile flows, icons, room creation/capacity, codes/deep links, direct joins, atomic slot assignment, lobby list, quick match, invite/observer entry, and observer permission boundaries. | AC-01–03, AC-20–28, AC-43, AC-46, AC-50–51. | Mock public read projections, identity verifier, room repository/transactions, and realtime interfaces; prove privacy filters, boundary and concurrency behavior before implementation. Exit with landing page available without login, cross-client integration tests, and no over-capacity race. |
| **3 — Lobby lifecycle and readiness** | Implement ordered membership, observer queue timestamps, pre-countdown vacancy promotion and roster compaction, ready state, 30-second idle prompt, holdout warning/removal, countdown start/lock, and no replacement after lock. | AC-24–28, AC-30–33 (plus AC-01/02 membership regression). | Use a fake clock and deterministic event scheduler. Mock multi-client events and simultaneous leave/ready/timeout operations. Exit only when boundary and race tests prove the roster invariant and locked-roster rule. |
| **4 — Curated content and core match/round engine** | Implement validated catalog loading; category art binding; roster snapshot and anchor draw; category choice; authoritative round progression and stage submissions; answer checking; scoring/time; solve locking; hint visibility; reveal; summaries and standings/tiebreak. | AC-04–16, AC-45. | Mock content repository, clock, random source, and concurrent submissions. Prove deterministic ordering, privacy, stage transitions, scoring, and result calculations against mocks first. Exit with service integration tests against a disposable Supabase environment. |
| **5 — Nominations, suggestions, reactions** | Implement no-hint nomination eligibility, normalization/counting, moderation gate and future-pool eligibility; 10-win unlock and three-pair category suggestion review; menu-limited emoji reactions and realtime delivery. | AC-17–19, AC-29, AC-47. | Mock auth, moderation roles, thresholds, content validation, and event transport. Exit with unauthorized, below-threshold, duplicate, rejected, and approved cases covered. |
| **6 — Responsive UX, accessibility, and complete acceptance validation** | Complete phone portrait/landscape behavior, keyboard/touch operation, contrast and focus states, loading/offline/quota/reconnect states; run end-to-end flows across landing, identity, lobby, game, and results; close all AC traceability gaps. | All 45 active ACs; retired IDs AC-34, AC-35, AC-36, AC-40, AC-48, and AC-49 are excluded from AC regression. | Browser tests use deterministic seeded data and mocked/intercepted external services as appropriate. Automated browser checks and independent agent visual/usability review cover representative phone-sized viewports in both orientations. Human feedback is optional and is not a coding-phase exit gate. No known acceptance criterion remains uncovered or failing. |
| **7 — Post-coding deployment and release** | Begins only after coding Phases 1–6 are complete and the full AC suite passes. Implement and run TR-only provisioning/build/SWBOM tools, confirm environment topology, provision Development/Staging/Production, connect Vercel Git integration, deploy and verify operations, package the complete GPL source archive with matching SWBOM, and publish. This phase performs operational configuration and release work; it adds no game features. | Final regression across all 45 active ACs; TR-20–TR-29 operational/build/release work. AC-41/42 verify source archive contents using temporary fixtures. | Validate mockable TR contracts before writing deployment tooling; then pass real account, integration and deployment checks separately. No deployment or Vercel Preview build occurs in coding Phases 1–6. Deployment checks and deployed artifacts never count as AC evidence. |

### Phase 0A test-harness bootstrap and Phase 1–6 execution packages

After Phase 0 approval, install only the direct dependencies listed in `ATTRIBUTIONS.md` that are needed to run tests; create the lockfile and minimal test-runner configuration; then author the contract tests, mocks/fakes, and fixtures. This bootstrap may add test-only configuration and test code, but no game domain behavior, UI, routes, database schema/migrations, production adapters, or deployment scripts. Run and record the complete mock suite for all 45 active ACs before starting Phase 1A. Phase 1A may then create the application skeleton and remaining production build/module configuration.

The phase table gives each phase's boundaries. This breakdown makes the implementation work reviewable and keeps production behavior within the approved AC contracts. The global active-AC mock-validation gate precedes all packages; each package then follows BDP v4 Red → Green → Refactor and closes with a full regression run.

| Phase / package | Work sequence | AC scope | Mock-first test focus | Exit evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1A — Application skeleton and module boundaries** | Create the Next.js/TypeScript application skeleton and context/module boundaries; configure application lint/type/build commands against the already validated test harness. | AC-38/39/51; TR-25/26. | Test manifest completeness, dependency/attribution consistency, and domain import boundaries with fixture manifests and mocked adapters. | Reproducible local setup; lockfile matches ATTRIBUTIONS; 45/45 ACs mapped to 67 executable test oracles; conforming/violating mock-trace gate recorded. Product behavior still requires real-SUT validation. |
| **1B — Domain and application ports** | Create typed domain/application interfaces for room, match, content, profile, clock, random source, deadline scheduler, quota, identity, and outbox. | AC-37/51; TR-01/03/08/22/31. | Contract failures, idempotency outcomes, conflict responses, outbox intent, deterministic time/random seams; mocks do not implement domain decisions. | Domain has no framework imports; all contract tests compile and pass against fakes before adapters. |
| **1C — Persistence security and migration baseline** | Implement initial schema, constraints, RLS, server-only Supabase adapter, transaction/RPC boundaries, outbox and idempotency persistence. | AC-28/37/47/51; TR-01/05/09/22/31. | Application contracts remain fake-backed; local DB integration separately proves RLS, atomic capacity, idempotency and outbox durability (TR only). | Migration/RLS checks pass on local disposable Postgres; no deployed service is used. |
| **2A — Anonymous landing projections** | Build rules, ranking and lobby read models with bounded paging, empty/unavailable states, cache intervals, and no-auth route. | AC-43/50; TR-30. | Mock projection data tests all field allowlists, ranking, alias/opt-out, guest opt-in, 5-minute leaderboard refresh, 15-second lobby refresh, rules version/date, pagination and cache policy. | Anonymous journey passes with synthetic projections; private data remains absent. |
| **2B — Identity and profiles** | Implement guest browser identity, generated aliases/opt-out/icon, OIDC callback/token validation and profile association. | AC-03/20/21/46. | Fake OIDC discovery/JWKS/claim failures; guest persistence and account isolation; no real credentials. | Authenticated and guest sessions pass local tests; secrets stay server-side. |
| **2C — Rooms and discovery** | Implement create/capacity/code, browse/quick-match, invites/deep links, observer entry, scoped views and read-only authorization. | AC-01/02/22–28/50/51. | Capacity boundaries, join conflicts, FIFO quick match, stable IDs, invitation binding, privacy, and concurrent seat claims. | Cross-client room integration tests against local DB/Realtime pass; database evidence remains TR. |
| **3A — Membership and observer ordering** | Implement ordered player membership, observer arrival sequence, pre-countdown promotion into final slot, roster compaction, stable-ID ties, reconnect grace and room expiry. | AC-24–28/30/51; TR-09/10/18/31. | Fixed clock and interleaved leave/join commands; no observer promotion after countdown lock. | Aggregate invariants pass; separate TR database race cases pass locally. |
| **3B — Readiness and deadlines** | Implement SetReady, idle prompt, holdout warning, timeout policy, countdown and lock, below-minimum abort/close. | AC-30–33. | Fake clock/scheduler at 30s/5s/10s; 2-player wait; >2-player removal; ready/leave/expiry races; stale version no-ops. | All readiness and departure state transitions pass unit/use-case tests and local persistence integration. |
| **4A — Catalog and match setup** | Validate curated records; choose category/background; snapshot roster; assign anchor by injected uniform random range; choose pair without repeat until category pool is exhausted. | AC-04/05/16. | Catalog invalid fixtures, random range boundaries, anchor authorization, category background, pair pool depletion/reshuffle. | Only complete approved content is playable; seeded match setup is deterministic under fakes. |
| **4B — Round engine and scoring** | Implement no-hint and hint stages, submission acceptance, stage timers, answer normalization, score lock, solve times, reveal and summaries. | AC-06–14/45. | All scoring stages, no response/no solver, Unicode normalization, exact accepted answer set, simultaneous submissions, no duplicate scoring, private guesses/hints and final ties. | Full deterministic round suite passes; local integration confirms persisted ordering separately. |
| **5A — Nominations and moderation** | Implement eligibility from no-hint solves, normalized unique nominations, threshold queue, moderator roles/reasons/appeal/audit, complete-record curation gate, and future-pool query. | AC-16–18/47. | 9/10 threshold, unique profile, duplicate/retry, unauthorized and self-review cases, one appeal with distinct Senior Moderator uphold/overturn outcomes, audit, incomplete/unapproved exclusion. | Moderation decisions are audited and only complete curated content can enter future play. |
| **5B — Suggestions and reactions** | Implement ten-lifetime-win unlock, one-open suggestion with three pairs, review/curation handoff, reaction menu, rate interval and expiry. | AC-19/29/47. | 9/10 wins, duplicate open suggestion, invalid pair count, approval ≠ publication, emoji allowlist, 2s/5s behavior, no state mutation. | Suggestion/reaction suites pass; no paid service is introduced. |
| **6A — Responsive and accessible UI** | Finish portrait/landscape layouts, touch/keyboard controls, focus, contrast, status labels/shapes, loading/quota/reconnect/error states. | AC-15/37/44. | Component tests plus browser viewport/keyboard cases; axe/contrast fixtures if selected dependency/license review allows. | All AC-44 assertions pass at phone viewports in both orientations. |
| **6B — Full acceptance and hostile validation** | Run full mocked AC suite, local DB/Realtime TR integrations, seeded multi-client browser journeys, agent visual/usability/accessibility review, adversarial/privacy review and final docs/receipt update. | All 45 active ACs; TR integration separate. | Re-run every AC test ID; no deployed artifact or live external account is used as AC evidence. | 45/45 active ACs green; TR evidence separated; Phase 6 hostile review ≥98/98; release-ready source, with deployment still deferred to Phase 7. |

### Post-coding deployment environments (topology finalized at Phase 7 entry)

The environment mapping below is a planning proposal. Confirm the branch-to-environment mapping, project allocation, account capacity, and service settings at Phase 7 entry, after coding Phases 1–6 are complete. These operational choices do not gate Phase 0 or change the AC contract expectations.

- **Development:** local Next.js and local test/mocked services; disposable Supabase project or isolated local database for integration testing where practical.
- **Staging:** a persistent Vercel Preview target (for example, a protected `staging` branch) and isolated Supabase project/configuration. Validate migrations, quotas, OIDC callback, and release packaging without Production data.
- **Production:** Vercel Production deployments from `main`, connected only to the Production Supabase project and production secrets.

Each environment has separately scoped credentials and Supabase/Vercel variables. Provisioning scripts must be repeatable and safe to rerun, print identifiers/status but never secret values, and make paid resource configuration impossible by default. Document free-plan limits and verify current account quotas at provisioning/release time.

## 4. Acceptance-criterion traceability

This is the approved allocation of every criterion to its first implementation phase. During the global mock-validation gate, replace each planned case ID with a concrete test-file/test-case identifier. A criterion may have multiple unit, integration, browser, and manual tests; it must have at least one automated assertion unless the approved criterion explicitly requires human-only evidence.

| Criteria | Increment | Minimum test evidence |

## 5. Global mock-validation gate and incremental TDD protocol

Phase 0 is approved. Before any production implementation code, author and mock-validate the complete contract-test suite for every active AC. Mockable TR contracts are validated before their respective implementation; deployment TR tooling is implemented only in post-coding Phase 7. Live deployment/account/database checks are TR-only integration or operational evidence and do not count as AC coverage. Once the global mock-validation gate passes, apply this sequence to each small coding increment:

1. **Select scope:** identify the approved requirement and AC IDs; state the behavior, invariant, and exclusions. Confirm no unresolved decision changes expected results.
2. **Design boundary:** identify the public interface and injected collaborators. For time, randomness, network, persistence, identity, and event delivery, define deterministic seams before test authoring.
3. **Write the AC-to-test mapping:** record at least one test case for each applicable AC and each important boundary case. Include negative/security cases and concurrent state changes when relevant.
4. **Build mocks/fakes:** provide executable mock adapters that represent the specified public contract. Keep assertions on observable behavior; do not let the mock implement the business rule being tested.
5. **Global pre-implementation mock-oracle validation:** before production code, execute all 67 AC oracles against conforming and violating scripted mock traces; every oracle must accept the conforming trace and reject its targeted mutation. This validates assertion sensitivity only. Record every test ID, command, result, and evidence boundary. Then run the same oracles against each real implementation increment and record product-conformance separately.
6. **TR-19 reaction-policy contracts:** keep `TR-19-T01` through `TR-19-T04` separate from AC coverage. Before reaction implementation, validate the complete emoji allowlist, exact five-second visibility, one-per-player-per-two-second rate rule, full player/observer audience, and game-state invariance against conforming and violating mock observations.
7. **Implement the smallest behavior:** after the global gate passes, use failing contracts as targets within a small increment. Avoid unrelated refactoring or scope additions.
8. **Run increment and regression suites:** run all tests for this increment plus all previous increments. Keep production integration separate from the mock contract tests.
9. **Integrate real adapters:** after unit tests pass, add integration tests against disposable/local services; only use test credentials and seeded data. Do not replace mock-first unit tests with integration-only coverage.
10. **Review evidence:** verify AC mapping, test output, security boundaries, accessibility, docs, migrations, and artifact effects. Update the matrix whenever requirements change.
11. **Close increment:** merge only when checks pass and the work is reviewable. Validate the branch locally and against disposable services. Vercel Preview deployment and its SWBOM occur only in Phase 7, after coding Phases 1–6 are complete. Record agent visual/usability review and any optional human feedback separately; a mandatory personal sign-off applies only if explicitly requested by the user.

Mock fidelity is reviewed: mocks implement the documented interface, model failures/timeouts and authorization results, and do not encode implementation internals. Use fixed clocks, seeded random sources, transaction fakes, event capture, and deterministic fixtures. Add contract tests to compare real adapters with the same interface so mocks cannot drift.

## 6. Proposed test architecture

| Layer | Purpose | Tools and boundaries |
|---|---|---|
| Domain/unit | Pure room, roster, ready, match, round, scoring, eligibility, and validation rules. | Vitest; fake clock/randomness; repository and publisher interfaces mocked. |
| Component | Accessible controls, lobby transitions, observer/read-only view, hints, scorecards, summaries, and error states. | React Testing Library and user-event; mock API/client events; jsdom. |
| Service/contract | Authorization, transactions, quota handling, identity validation, and Realtime event payload contracts. | Vitest/MSW; Supabase/OIDC adapters replaced by contract fakes; explicit commit/rollback tests. |
| Browser acceptance | Anonymous landing page, full player journeys, and responsive layout across guest/authenticated identities and multiple clients. | Playwright; deterministic data; network interception for OIDC and external services; local or Staging app. |
| Integration | Verify migrations, row-level security, transactions, persistence/reconnect, and Realtime behavior. | Disposable Supabase/local database project; seeded fixtures; never Production. |
| Optional human feedback | Game comprehension, mobile use, moderation experience, accessibility, and staging/release procedure. | Supplement automated and independent agent review where appropriate; findings tracked against AC/decisions. No mandatory personal sign-off for coding-phase exit. |

Every mock is initialized with deterministic clocks, IDs, and random values. Tests cover error and retry states as well as success. Never use real OIDC credentials, Production data, or paid services in automated tests. Preserve test output as build/release evidence.

## 7. Architecture and implementation order

### 7.1 Trust and authority

The browser is an untrusted presentation/client. A server-side application service owns membership, roster order, readiness, countdown transitions, answer validation, hint visibility, scoring, timestamps, category permissions, nomination eligibility, moderation state, and final ranking. Database constraints and transactions backstop service checks. Clients cannot choose trusted identity claims, promote themselves, assign points, reveal targets, alter the roster after lock, or mutate state through observer sessions.

Use a server-owned clock and injected random source. Assign a stable event/order key to simultaneous submissions and membership events. Persist the authoritative transition before broadcasting it. Realtime delivery is a view of committed state, not the source of truth. Define idempotency keys for joins, guesses, reactions, and moderation actions so retries do not duplicate side effects.

### 7.2 Suggested module boundaries

- `domain/`: typed entities, value objects, validation, state machines, scoring, and pure policies.
- `application/`: use cases and transaction orchestration; depends on interfaces only.
- `adapters/supabase/`: queries, migrations, transaction/RPC functions, row-level security, and Realtime transport.
- `adapters/identity/`: OIDC token verification and guest session issuance.
- `web/`: Next.js routes, server actions/API handlers, accessible React views, and client event subscriptions.
- `content/`: curated seed records and category backgrounds; validation runs at build and import.
- `tests/`: unit, component, service-contract, integration, and browser suites organized by AC ID.
- `scripts/`: provisioning, migration/status checks, SWBOM validation, release archive creation, and archive inspection. Scripts are safe to rerun and redact secrets.

This section preserves the original planning boundary map. The implemented layout uses `src/domain`, `src/application`, `src/infrastructure`, `src/web` and App Router entries under `src/app`; see [local development](local_development.md). Provisioning and operational release scripts in this planned map remain Phase 7 work.

### 7.3 Critical data invariants

- Active player count never exceeds room capacity (2–25); assignment is atomic under concurrency.
- A player appears once in an active roster; order is explicit and stable except the confirmed pre-countdown compaction rule.
- Promotion only occurs before countdown start, selects the earliest observer, places them last, shifts other players up without reordering them, and preserves remaining observers.
- Start countdown and roster lock happen atomically when all players are ready, or when an expired holdout is removed from a room with more than two players. In an exactly two-player room, expiry leaves the holdout in place and does not start the countdown. After lock, departures create a vacancy and never trigger replacement.
- A 30-second idle readiness prompt and 5-second holdout warning are driven from authoritative state/version timestamps, so stale timer callbacks cannot mutate a changed lobby.
- One accepted score per player per round; stage score is fixed at acceptance. Hints go only to players unsolved at the current transition.
- The target answer is never sent before reveal; incorrect guess text is never broadcast to other players or observers.
- Observer identity is bound to approved invite context; observer commands are read-only and scoreless.
- The landing page uses a public read-only projection with an allowlist of approved leaderboard/lobby fields; it cannot query private room state or mutate game state.
- OIDC authentication creates an authenticated profile only after server validation of the configured provider's signature and required claims.
- Moderation and catalog activation are separately authorized; candidate approval never directly makes incomplete content playable.
- Provisioning separates Preview/Staging and Production targets and can be safely repeated without exposing secrets or erasing user data.
- Domain policies are pure and framework-independent; each room mutation uses a transactional lock/version check, idempotency key, and same-transaction outbox event.
- Only approved, complete content records are playable; nominations/suggestions cannot bypass moderation or catalog validation.

## 8. Post-coding deployment, release, licensing, and SWBOM

This section applies only after coding Phases 1–6 are complete. Deployment is not part of those coding phases.

Vercel Git integration creates Preview deployments for non-production branches and Production deployments from `main`. Configure a persistent Staging Preview path plus Development and Production credentials. The app build command first runs the complete test suite. After tests pass, generate a CycloneDX JSON 1.6 SWBOM from the exact committed lockfile and Vercel build metadata, then build the app so the report is included at `public/sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json` in that immutable deployment. The report includes direct/transitive runtime and development components, declared licenses, package URLs, dependency relationships, build timestamp, commit SHA, deployment environment, and deployment URL; it contains no secrets.

For each release, a manual, reproducible packaging command obtains the SWBOM for the selected Production deployment and verifies schema, hash/commit identity, and required metadata. It creates a source archive containing the complete source for that release, root `LICENSE`, attribution notices, and the same report at `sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json`. Validate the archive contents and open/read the SWBOM before publishing the release. Fail closed if the report is missing, invalid, secret-bearing, or references a different commit. Do not substitute a newly generated report from a different dependency lockfile or a Preview deployment.

Before locking dependencies, review direct/transitive licenses and whether shipped browser bundles/assets constitute redistributed components. Planned Apache-2.0 developer/build tools must remain tooling-only; preserve their notices as required by their terms and do not bundle them as game runtime code. A SWBOM's declared license field is an inventory, not an automatic compatibility ruling. The attribution document must track all direct dependencies and externally sourced assets; refresh it and the SWBOM whenever dependency or asset inputs change.

## 9. Project risks and controls

| Risk | Control / proof required |
|---|---|
| Ambiguous rules cause rework or incompatible tests. | Resolve decisions before affected AC tests; update approved requirements and traceability first. |
| Timer/event races corrupt room state. | State-versioned deadlines, server clock, transactional transitions, deterministic race tests, idempotency. |
| Concurrent joins overfill rooms. | Atomic database reservation and concurrency integration tests; quick-match uses the same reservation path as direct join. |
| OIDC assumptions fail against the chosen provider. | Verify discovery metadata and token-validation contract in planning; mock success/failure first; no token trust from browser input. |
| Realtime exposes hidden answers or private guesses. | Explicit event allowlist and per-recipient projections; security tests assert secret fields are absent. |
| Free-tier pause/quota disrupts play. | Isolated quota adapter, recoverable UX, validate the fixed v2.6 target of one full 25-player room plus up to 25 observers during Phase 7 quota simulation; no paid fallback. |
| GPL conflict in runtime/transitive bundle or artwork. | Lockfile/SWBOM/license review before adding or shipping each component; preserve notices; release gate blocks unresolved licenses. |
| Mock differs from Supabase/OIDC behavior. | Adapter contract tests plus staged integration test suite after mock-first unit tests. |
| Build artifact and source archive describe different commits. | Embed commit SHA in SWBOM; verify deployment, source tag, lockfile, and archive all match before publication. |
| Context/process drift skips a gate. | Keep this plan, AC traceability, and per-increment evidence in the repo; each work item names AC IDs and mock-first gate. |

## 10. Completion definition

A coding increment is complete only when its approved ACs map to passing mock-first tests, implementation and regression suites pass, security/data invariants are verified, and migrations/interfaces are documented. Do not deploy during coding Phases 1–6. After those phases and the full active-AC suite complete, Phase 7 performs deployment, operational verification, and release packaging. Deployment checks and deployed artifacts remain outside AC coverage.

The global AC mock-oracle suite had 67 primary AC scenarios, 27 supplemental scenarios, four separate TR-19 cases and 112 named controls; its 316 tests passed independent exact-commit review at 99% accuracy / 100% completeness on `f7b5ff8302e24c6eae4dd1d2f21d7cba8577ac29`. Phases 1–6 subsequently implemented and independently validated the application, including gameplay. [Phase 6](phase6_execution.md) records formal coding completion. The later administration extension passed 502 unit/contract tests, 66 PostgreSQL tests, 31 browser journeys and the production build, with an independent 99/99 review. Those extension results supplement the historical baseline; they do not replace its recorded source-bound acceptance mapping or claim Phase 7 completion.

## Live transport follow-up

The phone stale-roster defect expanded the follow-up from lobby recovery to actual private delivery and autonomous progression. [The reviewed plan and execution evidence](room_sync_fix.md) cover real UI integration, scheduler failure handling, bounded publication, resume coalescing and lifecycle cleanup. The previous administration/PWA review receipts remain historical snapshots.

98	4. `provision production`: create or link the Production Supabase project; apply the same migration sequence after Staging validation; set only Production variables; require an explicit operator confirmation and verify the target project ID before applying.
99	5. `status`: show project IDs, regions, plan names, migration version, deployment branch mapping, and secret variable names/presence only.
100	6. `backup` / `restore-check`: create a database export to an operator-controlled encrypted location, record checksum and schema version, and restore it to a disposable local/Staging database to prove recoverability. Never commit dumps or retain them in a public artifact.
101	
102	The script obtains authentication from the operator's CLI session or environment. It must redact command output, avoid shell tracing of secrets, avoid placing credentials in command-line arguments where process listings may expose them, enforce restrictive file permissions on temporary files, and remove temporary files on success/failure. It is idempotent: reruns report already-correct state and do not reset projects or erase data. No script may silently change a plan or enable a paid feature.
103	
104	### 4.3 Infrastructure configuration under version control
105	
106	Store Supabase configuration, SQL migrations, seed fixtures, application build commands, and non-secret environment-variable names in the repo. Store no access token, database password, service-role key, OAuth client secret, user data, or exported database. Keep environment configuration as an allowlisted schema describing required key, target environments, public/private classification, and validation rule.
107	
108	Use a two-person review where possible; otherwise use an explicit self-review checklist for Production. Supabase schema and RLS policies are reviewed as code. Keep Vercel build configuration in the project files only where the framework actually requires it; do not duplicate settings in incompatible Dashboard and file-based configuration.
109	
110	## 5. Git-to-Vercel workflow (post-coding phase)
111	
112	Do not connect the repository to Vercel or execute deployments during coding Phases 1–6. Complete local and disposable-service validation first. Begin this workflow only in Phase 7, after the coding phase is complete and the full AC suite passes.
113	
114	### 5.1 Repository setup
115	
116	1. Connect the existing `sharpninja/wordpairs` repository to a Vercel Hobby project owned by the matching personal Vercel account.
117	2. Select the production branch `main`; verify the framework preset, root directory, install command, test/build command, and output handling from the implemented Next.js app.
118	3. Enable deployment comments/links where available. Review fork deployment authorization and Preview protection so an untrusted pull request cannot access secrets or run against Production.
119	4. Add Preview and Production environment variables with least privilege. Apply a branch-specific Preview override for `staging`; Preview defaults still point only to Staging/non-production infrastructure.
120	5. Enable Vercel-provided environment metadata needed by the build (commit SHA, branch, deployment URL/environment). Treat all build-time environment values as secrets unless explicitly classified as public.
121	6. Verify one feature branch Preview and one `main` Production deployment. Confirm the author rule and that no GitHub Actions workflow is involved.
122	7. Verify the anonymous landing-page route is reachable without authentication and returns only the public projection; inspect rendered HTML, network responses, cache headers, logs, and the SWBOM endpoint for accidental secrets or private lobby/game fields.
123	
124	### 5.2 Normal change path
125	
126	1. Start from current `main`; create a short-lived feature branch named for the work item and AC IDs.
127	2. Before implementation, pass the increment's mock-first TDD gate. The build cannot proceed if tests fail.
128	3. Push the branch. Vercel automatically builds a Preview. The build sequence is: install from lockfile → static/type/content checks → full test suite → generate and validate deployment SWBOM → production framework build including the SWBOM.
129	4. Validate the Preview URL, environment label, branch, commit, database target, and SWBOM endpoint. Execute acceptance/browser tests against synthetic staging data; review accessibility and log/errors.
130	5. Merge only after review and all gates. Vercel deploys the new `main` commit to Production. Migration ordering must be safe for old and new application revisions during rollout.
131	6. Run a post-deploy smoke checklist against the immutable Production deployment URL and canonical domain; inspect errors and quota dashboard. Do not run destructive tests against Production.
132	
133	### 5.3 Build command and gates
134	
135	The eventual package scripts should make the sequence explicit and exit non-zero on any failed gate. Exact command names are selected after dependency versions are validated and pinned.
136	
137	| Gate | Required checks | Failure behavior |
138	|---|---|---|
139	| Source | Clean lockfile install; type/lint/static analysis; curated content validation; verify generated files are deterministic. | Stop build. |
140	| Tests | Unit/component and all earlier increment suites; acceptance traceability report confirms all active ACs have tests; mock-first result is recorded. | Stop before SBOM/application build. |
141	| Supply-chain | Generate CycloneDX JSON 1.6 from the exact lockfile; include runtime and development/build dependencies and required metadata; validate schema, commit SHA, environment, deployment URL, and absence of secrets. | Stop build; do not deploy an artifact with missing or wrong metadata. |
142	| Application | Next.js production build; include report at `public/sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json`; verify exact endpoint path is part of output. | Vercel deployment fails. |
143	| Deployment | Verify Vercel environment and source commit; check expected Supabase project binding; run smoke checks, including anonymous landing-page and public-data privacy checks. | Do not promote/announce release; use rollback procedure if Production is degraded. |
144	
145	Every successful Preview and Production deployment serves its own immutable `/sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json`. Include the Vercel deployment URL, `VERCEL_ENV`, branch and commit metadata available at build time. Ensure metadata is escaped/validated and does not disclose environment variables. Preview and Production deployments from the same SHA still have distinct build/deployment metadata and each report belongs to the URL that serves it.
146	
147	## 6. Database migration and change strategy
148	
149	- Develop each migration locally or against a disposable database; run schema and RLS tests against mocks first, then the Supabase local stack or Staging.
150	- Keep migrations forward-compatible across the currently deployed and candidate application versions. Prefer expand → deploy compatible code → migrate/backfill → contract in later work. Do not drop/rename a live column in the same release that first stops reading it.
151	- Apply the same ordered migration set to Staging, then Production. Verify migration history/version before and after. A production migration command requires the selected project ID to match an allowlisted Production ID and a human confirmation.
152	- Seed only curated public content through reviewed, idempotent migration/seed files. Keep synthetic test accounts separate from real user data.
153	- Define transaction and lock behavior for online changes. Estimate table size and lock duration before applying any expensive migration under the Free database resource limit.
154	- Supabase Free currently lists a 500 MB database per project, 5 GB egress, 200 Realtime peak connections, 2 million Realtime messages/month, and pausing after a week of low activity; its pricing page also lists no automatic backups. The requirements additionally set 100 Realtime messages/second as an operating threshold. Treat all of these as hard ceilings and verify the live project dashboard before deployment; design a buffer below each ceiling and test the recoverable quota response.
155	- Because free automatic backups are not included in the current plan, operator-managed encrypted exports and restore drills are required before real user data is accepted. These exports are disaster-recovery copies, not releases, and must not be placed in GitHub, Vercel static output, or public artifacts.
156	
157	## 7. Observability and incident response
158	
159	### Signals to inspect
160	
161	- Vercel deployment status, build duration/failure, function errors/duration/invocation quotas, runtime logs, and current Hobby usage.
162	- Supabase project status/paused state, database/storage size, egress, Realtime concurrent connections/messages, authentication errors, migration history, and available logs/retention.
163	- Landing-page read-model health: leaderboard query age, discoverable/joinable lobby result count, empty-state rate, cache age, query errors, and public projection field allowlist. Do not log individual leaderboard identities beyond the approved operational need.
164	- Application-level counters: active rooms/players/observers, join failures, readiness timeouts, reconnect rates, state-transition conflicts, quota responses, and repeated client retries. Collect the minimum data needed; do not log raw guesses, tokens, secret values, or unnecessary identity data.
165	- SWBOM endpoint reachability and commit/deployment metadata for each deployment.
166	
167	Since the Free plans do not promise a production SLA and have limited log retention, the runbook relies on operator review and exported deployment evidence. Alerting must not create a paid external dependency. Establish user-facing status copy for service unavailable, capacity reached, maintenance, and paused Supabase project states.
168	
169	### Incident sequence
170	
171	1. Identify affected environment, commit SHA, and service status; preserve relevant non-sensitive logs and quota snapshots.
172	2. Stop further migrations/releases if data integrity or auth is uncertain. Never enable paid usage to recover service.
173	3. For a bad application deployment, redeploy/rollback to the last known-good immutable Vercel deployment using the Vercel-supported rollback/promotion mechanism; verify it points to a compatible schema.
174	4. For schema/data faults, use a reviewed forward repair migration or restore a verified encrypted export to a deliberate recovery target. Do not assume a Vercel code rollback reverses database changes.
175	5. For a quota or project pause, show recoverable status, follow the current Free-plan resume/quota instructions, and validate data integrity before reopening joins. Do not repeatedly issue requests that increase quota pressure.
176	6. Record impact, timeline, root cause, data-loss assessment, recovery actions, and prevention work in a private incident log; update this plan and relevant tests/ACs.
177	
178	## 8. Release and archive procedure
179	
180	1. Select a Production deployment with known commit SHA `S` and verify it passed all tests and post-deploy checks.
181	2. Retrieve the SWBOM from that exact deployment's `/sbom/S.cdx.json`; validate JSON/CycloneDX 1.6, build/deployment URL, branch, lockfile inventory, commit SHA, license inventory, and no-secret scan.
182	3. Check out the corresponding source tag/commit and build a source archive reproducibly. Include all source needed to modify/build the release, root `LICENSE`, `ATTRIBUTIONS.md`, required third-party notices, release metadata, and the exact SWBOM at `sbom/S.cdx.json`.
183	4. Exclude `.env*`, `.vercel/`, Supabase access tokens, local database files/dumps, cached credentials, and unrelated generated artifacts. Include project source/configuration and migrations needed to reproduce the release.
184	5. Inspect the archive listing and extract it to a clean temporary directory. Confirm one `LICENSE`, one matching report, expected SHA, and no secret-like files; rerun the archive validation against the extracted contents.
185	6. Publish the archive and checksum through the approved GitHub release method. No GitHub Actions asset generation is involved; the operator manually invokes the versioned packaging command and reviews its output.
186	7. Open the release archive after publication, compare its checksum to the local validated archive, download/extract it, and verify the SWBOM and GPL notice are present.
187	
188	The packaging script must be deterministic where practical: stable file ordering, normalized timestamps/ownership, and checksum recorded separately. It must fail closed on missing/malformed/mismatched SWBOM or license review. The Production build artifact and source tag must identify the same commit; never attach a newer SWBOM to an older source archive.
189	
190	## 9. Rollback and recovery objectives
191	
192	During Phase 0, set realistic recovery-time and recovery-point expectations suitable for the game and free plans. The following are proposed controls, not uptime guarantees:
193	
194	- **Application rollback:** keep the prior known-good Vercel deployment available; rollback code without changing database configuration. Validate current schema compatibility before rollback.
195	- **Database recovery:** establish an encrypted operator-held backup/export cadence and retention window before onboarding real users; prove restoration to Staging/local and document the expected data-loss window. Supabase Free lacks automatic backups according to the current pricing table, so no managed point-in-time recovery is assumed.
196	- **Secrets:** rotate compromised credentials in the provider dashboard/CLI, update only affected environment scopes, redeploy, then verify that old credentials are rejected. Do not place secret values in issue comments or logs.
197	- **Project pause:** maintain a documented resume procedure and owner contact path for the Supabase project. Reopening after pause requires database connection, migration status, auth, and Realtime smoke checks.
198	
199	## 10. Deployment acceptance checklist
200	
201	### Provisioning and security
202	
203	- [ ] Vercel Hobby use remains personal/non-commercial; repository owner and commit author comply with current Hobby Git rules.
204	- [ ] Supabase Staging and Production are separate Free projects; no third paid resource is configured.
205	- [ ] Environment variables are scoped correctly; Preview cannot reach Production; secrets are absent from Git, logs, static files, artifacts, and screenshots.
206	- [ ] Provisioning `plan` is non-mutating; rerun is idempotent; production apply is target-checked and confirmed; migrations match the reviewed source.
207	- [ ] Staging and Production recovery procedures and encrypted backup/restore check are documented.
208	
209	### Build and deployment
210	
211	- [ ] A feature branch gets a Preview; `main` gets Production; no GitHub Actions workflow is required.
212	- [ ] Build order runs checks/tests before SWBOM and app build; failed tests fail deployment.
213	- [ ] Preview uses Staging credentials; Production uses Production credentials; protected fork deployment cannot expose secrets.
214	- [ ] TR-27 operational check confirms each deployment serves the SWBOM for its exact commit, lockfile, environment, and URL without secret values; this is TR evidence, not AC coverage.
215	- [ ] Smoke checks confirm the anonymous landing page, approved leaderboard projection, discoverable/joinable lobby summary, rules content, identity, room creation/join, quota error handling, and expected environment labeling.
216	- [ ] AC-43 and AC-50 contract tests pass against local components with mocked public projections before implementation. Any deployed smoke check is diagnostic only and does not count toward AC coverage.
217	- [ ] TR-23/TR-26/TR-27 configuration, provisioning, build-gate, and SWBOM checks pass as TR-only evidence; they do not substitute for AC coverage.
218	
219	### Release archive
220	
221	- [ ] Source release archive contains the complete corresponding source, `LICENSE`, attribution notices, and the SWBOM from the matching Production deployment.
222	- [ ] Archive SWBOM SHA equals the source release SHA; archive listing/extraction and secret scan pass.
223	- [ ] Published archive checksum matches the validated local artifact; the release is manually verified after publication.
224	
225	## 11. Current official references
226	
227	Checked 26 October 2026; re-check at provisioning and release because plan rules and quotas may change.
228	
229	- [Vercel Git deployments](https://vercel.com/docs/git) — branch previews, production branch behavior, and Hobby author/repository restrictions.
230	- [Vercel environments](https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/environments) — Local, Preview, Production, and Preview deployment behavior.
231	- [Vercel environment variables](https://vercel.com/docs/environment-variables) — environment and branch-specific Preview variables.
232	- [Vercel Hobby plan](https://vercel.com/docs/plans/hobby) — personal, non-commercial use and Hobby limits.
233	- [Supabase pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing) — Free project limits, included quotas, and backup availability.
234	- [Supabase Free project pausing](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/free-project-pausing) — low activity pause behavior and recovery.
235	- [Supabase local development](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development) and [database migrations](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development/database-migrations) — local stack and versioned schema changes.
236	- [`SWBOM.md`](SWBOM.md) and [`ATTRIBUTIONS.md`](ATTRIBUTIONS.md) — project artifact and license-inventory contracts.
237	
238	## Temporary local validation
239	
240	The local Realtime gateway, independent scheduler and real browser integration are documented in [the live multiplayer extension](room_sync_fix.md). This temporary leased runtime preserves the game database and is not a Vercel/Supabase cloud deployment. A cloud deployment must provide an independent deadline/outbox trigger and verify actual private delivery before release; browser polling does not establish scheduler health.
