# Wordpairs Deployment and Release Plan

Current release override, 28 October 2026: [guest game and GitHub admin PWA](admin_pwa_release.md)
is the current identity and installation contract. Public play has no manifest or
installation controls; `/admin/manifest.webmanifest` and `/admin-sw.js` serve the
admin PWA. Only verified GitHub owner sharpninja may administer it; profile-ID
bootstrap and user delegation are inactive. Both existing Vercel projects use
their production target, with explicit reviewed-commit staging deployment before
production. Earlier Preview/public-PWA/OpenAI/bootstrap proposals below are
historical where they conflict with this override. No GitHub Actions are added.

**Status:** Hosted setup in progress; see [execution and current blockers](hosting_execution.md)
**Requirements baseline:** `word_association_game_requirements.md` v2.6  
**Implementation sequence:** `implementation_plan.md`  
**Hosting constraint:** Vercel Hobby and Supabase Free; no paid add-ons or fallback  
**Automation constraint:** no GitHub Actions

## 1. Purpose and scope

The operator selected two existing projects: `wordpairs` for logical Staging and
`wordpairs-j9jf` for Production. Each uses its own stable Vercel production-target
domain and matching isolated Supabase project. This supersedes the single-project
Staging Preview proposal below. The [execution record](hosting_execution.md)
documents the current server-only configuration, scheduler, migrations and evidence.

Phone home-screen installation is implemented in the [PWA extension](pwa_design.md). Production must serve the application, `/manifest.webmanifest`, `/sw.js`, `/offline.html` and `/icons/*` from the same HTTPS origin. Preserve the worker's no-cache/no-store JavaScript headers and root scope. Operational checks must install and relaunch on actual Android/iPhone devices, verify standalone `/play`, offline reconnect guidance and recovery online. Local Chromium diagnostics and iPhone user-agent tests do not establish a physical-device installation or a hosted release. No deployment was performed as part of adding PWA support.

This document defines how Wordpairs will be provisioned, built, deployed, operated, rolled back, and released under the project's current constraints. Deployment, provisioning, build/SWBOM, and environment-isolation checks are bound to technical requirements TR-20–TR-29, not to ACs. Any live deployment/account/database checks are TR-only integration or operational evidence and cannot satisfy the AC mock-coverage gate. The public landing behavior remains covered by active AC-43 and AC-50 tests against local components and mocked projections; deployed smoke checks are operational diagnostics only.

The system uses Vercel Git integration for deployment from `sharpninja/wordpairs` and Supabase Postgres/Realtime for durable and live room data. Next.js/TypeScript is the selected application stack recorded in the approved Phase 0 technical ADR. GitHub Actions is not used. Provisioning and release archive creation are manually invoked from an authenticated workstation. The build and release gates are implemented only after the project's planning and mock-first TDD gates pass.

![Vercel deployment workflow](word_association_vercel_deployment.svg)

## 2.1 TR-only verification, separate from AC coverage

The following contract tests are specified before implementation and validated against mocks before the corresponding scripts/build code is written. They do not add ACs or count toward AC coverage. Real Vercel, Supabase, and deployment checks run later as technical integration evidence.

| TR | Mock-first technical contract | Later TR-only integration/operational evidence |
|---|---|---|
| TR-20, TR-24 | `TR-20-T01` / `TR-24-T01`: fake Vercel configuration metadata verifies branch-to-Preview/Production mapping and no GitHub Actions dependency. | Verify the connected repository and branch settings in Vercel; this is not AC evidence. |
| TR-21 | `TR-21-T01`: configuration policy rejects paid tiers, add-ons, and metered resources. | Confirm actual account plan/eligibility and deployed resource settings before provisioning/release. |
| TR-22 | `TR-22-T01`: application ports handle repository/Realtime success, failure, retry, and stale-state responses without assuming process memory is durable. | Disposable Supabase integration verifies persistence, RLS, transactions, and Realtime behavior. |
| TR-23 | `TR-23-T01`–`TR-23-T03`: fake CLI/temp filesystem verifies idempotent create/link, migration reporting, Preview/Production variable separation, and secret redaction. | Run safe provisioning and migration checks against isolated Staging/Production targets. |
| TR-26 | `TR-26-T01`: fake test runner proves the build orchestrator fails closed on test failure and orders checks before build. | Inspect actual Vercel build command/configuration; operational evidence only. |
| TR-27 | `TR-27-T01`: fixture lockfile and mocked build metadata produce a valid CycloneDX 1.6 SWBOM in a temporary pre-deployment build output with no secrets. | Verify the real build/deployment inventory and served endpoint; this remains TR-only and is not AC coverage. |
| TR-28, TR-29 | `TR-28-T01` / `TR-29-T01`: temporary source archive with fixture SWBOM/license verifies exact-commit paths and required notices. | Inspect the release archive and publication record; AC-41/42 also have independent mock-backed archive tests. |

## 2. Deployment principles and constraints

1. **No paid usage:** keep Vercel on Hobby and Supabase on Free. Never add a card-backed resource, paid add-on, metered service, or automatic paid fallback. A quota error is a recoverable application state, not permission to spend.
2. **Hobby is personal/non-commercial:** Vercel documents Hobby as personal, non-commercial use. Confirm continued eligibility before launch and whenever the project's use changes. If use becomes commercial, this deployment target no longer satisfies the requirement; stop and revise the hosting decision before continuing.
3. **Repository and author requirements:** the repo is public under the `sharpninja` account. Keep Vercel connected to the matching personal Git provider account. Vercel's current Hobby Git rules require the commit author to own the destination Hobby team; verify this on the first deployment and after changing Git identities. Private repositories in GitHub organizations are not deployable to Hobby under current Vercel rules.
4. **Environment separation:** local Development, Vercel Preview/Staging, and Vercel Production must use distinct secrets and data. Never pass Production credentials to a Preview deployment.
5. **Git is the deployment trigger:** pushes to non-production branches produce Preview deployments; pushes/merges to `main` produce Production deployments. Do not add a second deploy trigger that can race or bypass the approved path.
6. **Migrations are versioned:** schema changes live in reviewed migration files. No manual dashboard schema edits in a hosted environment; make any emergency repair immediately reproducible in a migration.
7. **Deployment is not a release:** every Vercel build has its own SWBOM. A public release additionally requires a source archive containing the same Production build's SWBOM and the complete GPL license.
8. **Landing-page data is public by design:** expose only an explicit, approved read model for leaderboard and discoverable lobby metadata. A landing-page query is never a shortcut to the private room API.

Vercel and Supabase plans, quotas, CLI behavior, and terms can change. This plan records a baseline checked on 26 October 2026 and requires a fresh official-doc/account-dashboard check before provisioning and each release. The values below are planning constraints, not a guarantee of future quotas.

## 3. Environments and data boundaries

| Environment | Hosting and branch | Database | Data and access rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Development** | Local Next.js server; local Supabase stack where the developer has a compatible container runtime. | Local disposable database; deterministic seeded content. | Mocked external services for unit/component tests; no Production data or credentials. `.env.local` and `.vercel/` are ignored by Git. |
| **Staging** | Persistent non-production branch (proposed name: `staging`) deploys to Vercel Preview. | Dedicated Supabase Free project. | Synthetic profiles, rooms, content, and test sessions only. Protect the Preview URL with Vercel's available deployment protection; reviewer access is explicitly granted. |
| **Feature Preview** | Each non-production branch/PR receives an immutable Vercel Preview URL. | Default to the Staging Supabase project with per-test unique identifiers; allow a branch-specific override only when a separately approved free project exists. | No Production secrets/data. Use branch-specific Vercel Preview variables to target `staging`; feature branches inherit the safe Preview defaults. Ensure tests clean up only their own seeded rows. |
| **Production** | Vercel Production deployments from `main`. | Dedicated Production Supabase Free project. | Real users/data; least-privilege keys; change control and release verification. Never use this environment for automated acceptance or destructive tests. |

Vercel Hobby currently provides Local, Preview, and Production environments; named custom environments are documented for Pro/Enterprise. Therefore “Staging” is a persistent protected Preview branch and isolated Supabase project, not a paid custom Vercel environment. Branch-specific Preview variables allow that branch to use its staging database while other Preview deployments inherit the non-production default. Local Supabase development is free but requires a Docker API-compatible container runtime; if unavailable, use mock-backed tests and do integration checks in Staging with strictly synthetic data.

Supabase Free currently permits two free projects across an owner's/admin's organizations. Allocate those projects to Staging and Production; confirm account availability before provisioning. Do not create a new hosted Supabase project for each branch. Make branch previews data-safe through opaque test prefixes, short-lived fixtures, cleanup scoped to the fixture owner, and no assumption that the shared staging database is empty.

## 4. Provisioning plan

### Administration configuration

Apply migration `010_access_control.sql` before using the [administration/ACL extension](admin_acl_design.md). Set `WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS` only in the server environment to a comma-separated list of existing profile IDs. The authenticated profile panel shows the current ID. Never use a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variable for this setting and never set it from browser input. Restart/redeploy when changing the allowlist. An empty value grants no bootstrap authority; there is no default administrator account or password. Persisted grants can then be managed at `/admin/users` by an effective administrator. Use durable signed-in profiles for operational administrators; losing guest browser data loses access to that guest identity. Separate Preview and Production administrator lists and databases.

### 4.1 Preconditions

- Confirm repository visibility, owner, production branch (`main`), expected commit author, and Vercel Hobby eligibility.
- Confirm the Vercel account/team and Supabase account have access to the personal GitHub repository and room for two Free projects.
- Review current official plan terms, usage quotas, project pausing, log retention, database backup availability, region choice, and CLI versions.
- Choose a region based on expected player geography and service availability; record the choice. Avoid claiming a multi-region or uptime guarantee on Free.
- Approve secret names and ownership without writing secret values to this plan or the repository.
- Approve database schema and migrations in accordance with the implementation plan. Deployment planning may be completed during Phase 0. Provisioning, deployment tooling, and deployment execution begin only after coding Phases 1–6 are complete, in Phase 7. Confirm branch/project topology at Phase 7 deployment entry.

### 4.2 Repeatable provisioning command

Implement one manually invoked PowerShell provisioning entry point, backed by pinned Supabase CLI and Vercel CLI versions. The current schema planner is `scripts/hosting-schema.ps1`; the earlier Node fallback is retired. Declare tools as direct development/build dependencies or provide a pinned documented installation mechanism, and add their purpose, license, and upstream source to `ATTRIBUTIONS.md`. Final branch/project topology and account-capacity confirmation are Phase 7 deployment-entry decisions after coding, not Phase 0 exit gates.

The command has explicit subcommands, a safe default dry-run/plan mode, and confirmation for destructive changes:

1. `doctor`: report CLI versions, linked accounts/project IDs, repository/branch, and required variable *names*; never print token or secret values.
2. `plan`: show the intended project/environment/migration/variable actions without mutation. Fail if the selected project plan is not Free, if a target project is ambiguous, or if an action could point Preview at Production.
3. `provision staging`: create or link the Staging Supabase project and Vercel project configuration; apply approved migrations; set only Preview variables, using a branch-specific override for `staging`; verify the settings without echoing values.
4. `provision production`: create or link the Production Supabase project; apply the same migration sequence after Staging validation; set only Production variables; require an explicit operator confirmation and verify the target project ID before applying.
5. `status`: show project IDs, regions, plan names, migration version, deployment branch mapping, and secret variable names/presence only.
6. `backup` / `restore-check`: create a database export to an operator-controlled encrypted location, record checksum and schema version, and restore it to a disposable local/Staging database to prove recoverability. Never commit dumps or retain them in a public artifact.

The script obtains authentication from the operator's CLI session or environment. It must redact command output, avoid shell tracing of secrets, avoid placing credentials in command-line arguments where process listings may expose them, enforce restrictive file permissions on temporary files, and remove temporary files on success/failure. It is idempotent: reruns report already-correct state and do not reset projects or erase data. No script may silently change a plan or enable a paid feature.

### 4.3 Infrastructure configuration under version control

Store Supabase configuration, SQL migrations, seed fixtures, application build commands, and non-secret environment-variable names in the repo. Store no access token, database password, service-role key, OAuth client secret, user data, or exported database. Keep environment configuration as an allowlisted schema describing required key, target environments, public/private classification, and validation rule.

Use a two-person review where possible; otherwise use an explicit self-review checklist for Production. Supabase schema and RLS policies are reviewed as code. Keep Vercel build configuration in the project files only where the framework actually requires it; do not duplicate settings in incompatible Dashboard and file-based configuration.

## 5. Git-to-Vercel workflow (post-coding phase)

Do not connect the repository to Vercel or execute deployments during coding Phases 1–6. Complete local and disposable-service validation first. Begin this workflow only in Phase 7, after the coding phase is complete and the full AC suite passes.

### 5.1 Repository setup

1. Connect the existing `sharpninja/wordpairs` repository to a Vercel Hobby project owned by the matching personal Vercel account.
2. Select the production branch `main`; verify the framework preset, root directory, install command, test/build command, and output handling from the implemented Next.js app.
3. Enable deployment comments/links where available. Review fork deployment authorization and Preview protection so an untrusted pull request cannot access secrets or run against Production.
4. Add Preview and Production environment variables with least privilege. Apply a branch-specific Preview override for `staging`; Preview defaults still point only to Staging/non-production infrastructure.
5. Enable Vercel-provided environment metadata needed by the build (commit SHA, branch, deployment URL/environment). Treat all build-time environment values as secrets unless explicitly classified as public.
6. Verify one feature branch Preview and one `main` Production deployment. Confirm the author rule and that no GitHub Actions workflow is involved.
7. Verify the anonymous landing-page route is reachable without authentication and returns only the public projection; inspect rendered HTML, network responses, cache headers, logs, and the SWBOM endpoint for accidental secrets or private lobby/game fields.

### 5.2 Normal change path

1. Start from current `main`; create a short-lived feature branch named for the work item and AC IDs.
2. Before implementation, pass the increment's mock-first TDD gate. The build cannot proceed if tests fail.
3. Push the branch. Vercel automatically builds a Preview. The build sequence is: install from lockfile → static/type/content checks → full test suite → generate and validate deployment SWBOM → production framework build including the SWBOM.
4. Validate the Preview URL, environment label, branch, commit, database target, and SWBOM endpoint. Execute acceptance/browser tests against synthetic staging data; review accessibility and log/errors.
5. Merge only after review and all gates. Vercel deploys the new `main` commit to Production. Migration ordering must be safe for old and new application revisions during rollout.
6. Run a post-deploy smoke checklist against the immutable Production deployment URL and canonical domain; inspect errors and quota dashboard. Do not run destructive tests against Production.

### 5.3 Build command and gates

The eventual package scripts should make the sequence explicit and exit non-zero on any failed gate. Exact command names are selected after dependency versions are validated and pinned.

| Gate | Required checks | Failure behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Source | Clean lockfile install; type/lint/static analysis; curated content validation; verify generated files are deterministic. | Stop build. |
| Tests | Unit/component and all earlier increment suites; acceptance traceability report confirms all active ACs have tests; mock-first result is recorded. | Stop before SBOM/application build. |
| Supply-chain | Generate CycloneDX JSON 1.6 from the exact lockfile; include runtime and development/build dependencies and required metadata; validate schema, commit SHA, environment, deployment URL, and absence of secrets. | Stop build; do not deploy an artifact with missing or wrong metadata. |
| Application | Next.js production build; include report at `public/sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json`; verify exact endpoint path is part of output. | Vercel deployment fails. |
| Deployment | Verify Vercel environment and source commit; check expected Supabase project binding; run smoke checks, including anonymous landing-page and public-data privacy checks. | Do not promote/announce release; use rollback procedure if Production is degraded. |

Every successful Preview and Production deployment serves its own immutable `/sbom/<commit-sha>.cdx.json`. Include the Vercel deployment URL, `VERCEL_ENV`, branch and commit metadata available at build time. Ensure metadata is escaped/validated and does not disclose environment variables. Preview and Production deployments from the same SHA still have distinct build/deployment metadata and each report belongs to the URL that serves it.

## 6. Database migration and change strategy

- Develop each migration locally or against a disposable database; run schema and RLS tests against mocks first, then the Supabase local stack or Staging.
- Keep migrations forward-compatible across the currently deployed and candidate application versions. Prefer expand → deploy compatible code → migrate/backfill → contract in later work. Do not drop/rename a live column in the same release that first stops reading it.
- Apply the same ordered migration set to Staging, then Production. Verify migration history/version before and after. A production migration command requires the selected project ID to match an allowlisted Production ID and a human confirmation.
- Seed only curated public content through reviewed, idempotent migration/seed files. Keep synthetic test accounts separate from real user data.
- Define transaction and lock behavior for online changes. Estimate table size and lock duration before applying any expensive migration under the Free database resource limit.
- Supabase Free currently lists a 500 MB database per project, 5 GB egress, 200 Realtime peak connections, 2 million Realtime messages/month, and pausing after a week of low activity; its pricing page also lists no automatic backups. The requirements additionally set 100 Realtime messages/second as an operating threshold. Treat all of these as hard ceilings and verify the live project dashboard before deployment; design a buffer below each ceiling and test the recoverable quota response.
- Because free automatic backups are not included in the current plan, operator-managed encrypted exports and restore drills are required before real user data is accepted. These exports are disaster-recovery copies, not releases, and must not be placed in GitHub, Vercel static output, or public artifacts.

## 7. Observability and incident response

### Signals to inspect

- Vercel deployment status, build duration/failure, function errors/duration/invocation quotas, runtime logs, and current Hobby usage.
- Supabase project status/paused state, database/storage size, egress, Realtime concurrent connections/messages, authentication errors, migration history, and available logs/retention.
- Landing-page read-model health: leaderboard query age, discoverable/joinable lobby result count, empty-state rate, cache age, query errors, and public projection field allowlist. Do not log individual leaderboard identities beyond the approved operational need.
- Application-level counters: active rooms/players/observers, join failures, readiness timeouts, reconnect rates, state-transition conflicts, quota responses, and repeated client retries. Collect the minimum data needed; do not log raw guesses, tokens, secret values, or unnecessary identity data.
- SWBOM endpoint reachability and commit/deployment metadata for each deployment.

Since the Free plans do not promise a production SLA and have limited log retention, the runbook relies on operator review and exported deployment evidence. Alerting must not create a paid external dependency. Establish user-facing status copy for service unavailable, capacity reached, maintenance, and paused Supabase project states.

### Incident sequence

1. Identify affected environment, commit SHA, and service status; preserve relevant non-sensitive logs and quota snapshots.
2. Stop further migrations/releases if data integrity or auth is uncertain. Never enable paid usage to recover service.
3. For a bad application deployment, redeploy/rollback to the last known-good immutable Vercel deployment using the Vercel-supported rollback/promotion mechanism; verify it points to a compatible schema.
4. For schema/data faults, use a reviewed forward repair migration or restore a verified encrypted export to a deliberate recovery target. Do not assume a Vercel code rollback reverses database changes.
5. For a quota or project pause, show recoverable status, follow the current Free-plan resume/quota instructions, and validate data integrity before reopening joins. Do not repeatedly issue requests that increase quota pressure.
6. Record impact, timeline, root cause, data-loss assessment, recovery actions, and prevention work in a private incident log; update this plan and relevant tests/ACs.

## 8. Release and archive procedure

1. Select a Production deployment with known commit SHA `S` and verify it passed all tests and post-deploy checks.
2. Retrieve the SWBOM from that exact deployment's `/sbom/S.cdx.json`; validate JSON/CycloneDX 1.6, build/deployment URL, branch, lockfile inventory, commit SHA, license inventory, and no-secret scan.
3. Check out the corresponding source tag/commit and build a source archive reproducibly. Include all source needed to modify/build the release, root `LICENSE`, `ATTRIBUTIONS.md`, required third-party notices, release metadata, and the exact SWBOM at `sbom/S.cdx.json`.
4. Exclude `.env*`, `.vercel/`, Supabase access tokens, local database files/dumps, cached credentials, and unrelated generated artifacts. Include project source/configuration and migrations needed to reproduce the release.
5. Inspect the archive listing and extract it to a clean temporary directory. Confirm one `LICENSE`, one matching report, expected SHA, and no secret-like files; rerun the archive validation against the extracted contents.
6. Publish the archive and checksum through the approved GitHub release method. No GitHub Actions asset generation is involved; the operator manually invokes the versioned packaging command and reviews its output.
7. Open the release archive after publication, compare its checksum to the local validated archive, download/extract it, and verify the SWBOM and GPL notice are present.

The packaging script must be deterministic where practical: stable file ordering, normalized timestamps/ownership, and checksum recorded separately. It must fail closed on missing/malformed/mismatched SWBOM or license review. The Production build artifact and source tag must identify the same commit; never attach a newer SWBOM to an older source archive.

## 9. Rollback and recovery objectives

During Phase 0, set realistic recovery-time and recovery-point expectations suitable for the game and free plans. The following are proposed controls, not uptime guarantees:

- **Application rollback:** keep the prior known-good Vercel deployment available; rollback code without changing database configuration. Validate current schema compatibility before rollback.
- **Database recovery:** establish an encrypted operator-held backup/export cadence and retention window before onboarding real users; prove restoration to Staging/local and document the expected data-loss window. Supabase Free lacks automatic backups according to the current pricing table, so no managed point-in-time recovery is assumed.
- **Secrets:** rotate compromised credentials in the provider dashboard/CLI, update only affected environment scopes, redeploy, then verify that old credentials are rejected. Do not place secret values in issue comments or logs.
- **Project pause:** maintain a documented resume procedure and owner contact path for the Supabase project. Reopening after pause requires database connection, migration status, auth, and Realtime smoke checks.

## 10. Deployment acceptance checklist

### Provisioning and security

- [ ] Vercel Hobby use remains personal/non-commercial; repository owner and commit author comply with current Hobby Git rules.
- [ ] Supabase Staging and Production are separate Free projects; no third paid resource is configured.
- [ ] Environment variables are scoped correctly; Preview cannot reach Production; secrets are absent from Git, logs, static files, artifacts, and screenshots.
- [ ] Provisioning `plan` is non-mutating; rerun is idempotent; production apply is target-checked and confirmed; migrations match the reviewed source.
- [ ] Staging and Production recovery procedures and encrypted backup/restore check are documented.

### Build and deployment

- [ ] A feature branch gets a Preview; `main` gets Production; no GitHub Actions workflow is required.
- [ ] Build order runs checks/tests before SWBOM and app build; failed tests fail deployment.
- [ ] Preview uses Staging credentials; Production uses Production credentials; protected fork deployment cannot expose secrets.
- [ ] TR-27 operational check confirms each deployment serves the SWBOM for its exact commit, lockfile, environment, and URL without secret values; this is TR evidence, not AC coverage.
- [ ] Smoke checks confirm the anonymous landing page, approved leaderboard projection, discoverable/joinable lobby summary, rules content, identity, room creation/join, quota error handling, and expected environment labeling.
- [ ] AC-43 and AC-50 contract tests pass against local components with mocked public projections before implementation. Any deployed smoke check is diagnostic only and does not count toward AC coverage.
- [ ] TR-23/TR-26/TR-27 configuration, provisioning, build-gate, and SWBOM checks pass as TR-only evidence; they do not substitute for AC coverage.

### Release archive

- [ ] Source release archive contains the complete corresponding source, `LICENSE`, attribution notices, and the SWBOM from the matching Production deployment.
- [ ] Archive SWBOM SHA equals the source release SHA; archive listing/extraction and secret scan pass.
- [ ] Published archive checksum matches the validated local artifact; the release is manually verified after publication.

## 11. Current official references

Checked 26 October 2026; re-check at provisioning and release because plan rules and quotas may change.

- [Vercel Git deployments](https://vercel.com/docs/git) — branch previews, production branch behavior, and Hobby author/repository restrictions.
- [Vercel environments](https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/environments) — Local, Preview, Production, and Preview deployment behavior.
- [Vercel environment variables](https://vercel.com/docs/environment-variables) — environment and branch-specific Preview variables.
- [Vercel Hobby plan](https://vercel.com/docs/plans/hobby) — personal, non-commercial use and Hobby limits.
- [Supabase pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing) — Free project limits, included quotas, and backup availability.
- [Supabase Free project pausing](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/free-project-pausing) — low activity pause behavior and recovery.
- [Supabase local development](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development) and [database migrations](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development/database-migrations) — local stack and versioned schema changes.
- [`SWBOM.md`](SWBOM.md) and [`ATTRIBUTIONS.md`](ATTRIBUTIONS.md) — project artifact and license-inventory contracts.

## Temporary local validation

The local Realtime gateway, independent scheduler and real browser integration are documented in [the live multiplayer extension](room_sync_fix.md). This temporary leased runtime preserves the game database and is not a Vercel/Supabase cloud deployment. A cloud deployment must provide an independent deadline/outbox trigger and verify actual private delivery before release; browser polling does not establish scheduler health.

1	# Administration and access control
2	
3	> Current release policy (28 October 2026): [Guest game and GitHub admin PWA](admin_pwa_release.md) supersedes the public-install/OpenAI/multi-account delegation scope below. Public play is guest-only; only verified sharpninja administers through GitHub, and only admin remains installable. The following original design and approval evidence is historical and does not approve the changed release.
4	
5	
6	Implementation extension requested 27 October 2026, after the completed Phase 0–6 baseline. Historical phase approvals remain historical evidence; this extension receives its own hostile validation.
7	
8	## Screens and operations
9	
10	`/admin` provides a searchable moderation queue with pending, appealed, approved and completed filters, reasoned approval/rejection, independent appeal resolution, complete curation forms and decision history. `/admin/words` provides category/search filters, pair creation and editing (prompt, target, accepted alternatives and exactly three ordered hints), and exclusion from future rounds with a reason. `/admin/users` provides profile search, current roles, audited grants/revocations and role history. Ordinary players receive an access-denied state; private data is never fetched through an unrestricted admin endpoint.
11	
12	## Permissions
13	
14	| Role | Moderate and curate | Author/edit pairs and hints | Resolve appeals | Assign/revoke roles |
15	|---|---|---|---|---|
16	| Player | No | No | No | No |
17	| Moderator | Yes | Yes | No | No |
18	| Senior moderator | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
19	| Administrator | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
20	
21	Appeal reviewers must remain independent of the proposer and original reviewer, even when they are administrators. Roles are additive; revoking one role does not revoke another role's permissions. The default player role cannot be assigned or removed. There is no browser-side self-grant or public administrator-bootstrap endpoint.
22	
23	## Server configuration and identity
24	
25	`WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS` is a server-only comma-separated list of existing, stable profile IDs. It is never exposed as a public environment variable or accepted in HTTP input. The authenticated profile screen displays the current profile ID so an operator can configure the first administrator. Configured administrators receive the admin role in trusted identity/content composition and SQL access checks; the entire allowlist is never returned to a client. Their administrator permission cannot be revoked through the UI. Changing the allowlist requires restarting/redeploying the server. Other administrator and moderator grants persist in PostgreSQL and are reloaded on every authenticated request.
26	
27	## Transaction boundaries
28	
29	### Permission-aware navigation
30	
31	`FR-ADMINPAGES-023/FR-23-C05` requires administration links to follow the same
32	permission matrix. The private, no-store session response projects only the
33	current actor's effective permissions; it never exports the bootstrap allowlist,
34	provider subject or server role context. Anonymous and ordinary player sessions
35	render no administration links, including on direct `/admin` entry. Moderators
36	can navigate to moderation and word pairs/hints; only administrators see users
37	and access. Existing route/application/SQL checks remain authoritative for every
38	read and write.
39	
40	The identity panel refreshes permissions every15 seconds and on tab focus.
41	Failed refreshes remove links. Session mutations retire prior reads and clear
42	navigation immediately; focus/poll refreshes cannot overtake a pending guest
43	entry or sign-out. Successful guest entry reloads the verified session before
44	showing any permission-based links. Missing permission fields fail closed.
45	`tests/browser/auth-navigation.phase6.spec.ts` covers the rendered role matrix,
46	direct entry, revocation, failure and logout. Deferred POST/DELETE regressions in
47	`tests/web/identity-navigation.test.ts` verify focus cannot restore an old session.
48	
49	
50	```mermaid
51	flowchart LR
52	    UI[Admin pages] --> HTTP[Authenticated route handlers]
53	    HTTP --> ACL[Access service]
54	    HTTP --> Content[Content service]
55	    Env[Server-only admin profile IDs] --> Identity[Trusted identity and role context]
56	    Identity --> ACL
57	    Identity --> Content
58	    ACL --> Exclusive[Exclusive ACL transaction lock]
59	    Content --> Shared[Shared ACL transaction lock]
60	    Exclusive --> Roles[(Roles, revision, retry records, audit)]
61	    Shared --> Fresh[Reload authoritative roles]
62	    Fresh --> Catalog[(Moderation aggregate, immutable catalog, audit, outbox)]
63	```
64	
65	The ACL has a singleton revision and a dedicated serialized change transaction. Only a current administrator can read the user directory or change roles. A role change validates the target profile, role, grant/revoke intent, reason, command ID, digest and expected ACL revision; it atomically writes the role, revision, canonical retry result and append-only audit record. Changed command digests and stale revisions reject. Removing the final effective administrator is rejected, considering configured administrators whose profiles exist. Concurrent cross-revocations serialize so they cannot remove every administrator. Revoked actors cannot use old ACL commands to regain authority.
66	
67	ACL mutations take an exclusive advisory transaction lock; privileged content mutations take the corresponding shared lock before loading authoritative roles. This establishes a single order for content writes racing with revocation. Content then follows the existing room/match/moderation/catalog lock order. Revocation denies new privileged commands; an exact replay of an already committed content command retains its existing mutation-free canonical response.
68	
69	Database functions are executable only by `service_role`. ACL tables have RLS enabled and deny browser roles, and privileged changes never depend on roles, wins or actor IDs supplied by the client. HTTP mutation routes require the canonical same-origin checks, a valid session, expected profile binding, strict field allowlists and no-store responses. Search results are bounded and include only profile ID, generated alias, identity kind and effective roles; they exclude credentials, email and OIDC subjects.
70	
71	## Catalog integrity
72	
73	Edits append the next immutable version of an existing pair; creation uses a new ID at version zero. Existing pair IDs cannot move between categories. All saves require a reason, valid approved category/background, bounded plain text, accepted alternatives and exactly three hints. The existing moderation aggregate serializes publication, audits, exclusions and catalog-revision invalidation in one database transaction. New records flow through the existing catalog projection trigger.
74	
75	Community activation creates only previously unused pair IDs at version zero. It cannot reuse an existing pair ID in another category or skip versions; revisions belong to the editorial save path.
76	
77	Active rounds continue using their original pair ID and version. Future pools choose the highest version per pair ID and include it only if that version is selectable; excluding it never falls back to an older version. Exclusion preserves historical records and cannot empty an initial category. A revised excluded pair is a new selectable version; older exclusions remain in history. Direct editorial authoring is a privileged, audited operation; community proposals continue through the existing independent review and activation workflow and cannot have their status silently overridden. There is no destructive delete operation.
78	
79	The existing catalog ceiling counts every approved historical pair version. Under the serialized moderation transaction, both direct saves and community activations must check the projected total before publishing: adding beyond 4096 versions returns `SERVICE_LIMIT` without state, audit, revision or idempotency writes. This includes editing an existing pair at the ceiling. A rejected edit leaves historical lookups and active games available.
80	
81	## Validation
82	
83	Pure policy and transport tests cover permission inheritance, configured administrators, input/identity/origin forgery, content revisions and invalid hints. Real PostgreSQL tests cover role grants, revocations, idempotency, concurrent final-administrator removal, role changes racing with content, audit atomicity, browser-role denial, immutable old content and new-round selection. Browser tests exercise ordinary-player denial, administrator role management, moderation, editable word/hint forms, uncertain retry and phone layout. Existing unit, integration, browser, type, lint and production-build checks remain applicable. Independent hostile review examines the design and the exact final change/evidence, and records unresolved findings rather than inventing user sign-off gates.
84	
85	## UI workflow extension
86	
87	The [UI implementation design and evidence](testing/ui/implementation.md) extends the existing authority and immutable-catalog boundary with reasoned changes_requested/resubmit and on_hold/resume transitions. Migration011 retains legacy pending records while adding pending_review and extending the one-open-suggestion index. The proposer-only revision path never bypasses independent review, curation or the rejection appeal policy. Actor, prior/new proposal, case version, reason and status are committed in the same audit transaction.
88	
89	Tab-local drafts, verified session generations, native profile Save/Cancel/Escape, canonical uncertain-command retention and acknowledged success results now survive authorized in-tab navigation. Authorization denial invalidates older reads before private data can return. The existing live room transport remains separately verified; fixture browser UI evidence does not establish the full real private-push player-count matrix.

This includes editing an existing pair at the ceiling. A rejected edit leaves historical lookups and active games available.

## Validation

Pure policy and transport tests cover permission inheritance, configured administrators, input/identity/origin forgery, content revisions and invalid hints. Real PostgreSQL tests cover role grants, revocations, idempotency, concurrent final-administrator removal, role changes racing with content, audit atomicity, browser-role denial, immutable old content and new-round selection. Browser tests exercise ordinary-player denial, administrator role management, moderation, editable word/hint forms, uncertain retry and phone layout. Existing unit, integration, browser, type, lint and production-build checks remain applicable. Independent hostile review examines the design and the exact final change/evidence, and records unresolved findings rather than inventing user sign-off gates.

## UI workflow extension

The [UI implementation design and evidence](testing/ui/implementation.md) extends the existing authority and immutable-catalog boundary with reasoned changes_requested/resubmit and on_hold/resume transitions. Migration011 retains legacy pending records while adding pending_review and extending the one-open-suggestion index. The proposer-only revision path never bypasses independent review, curation or the rejection appeal policy. Actor, prior/new proposal, case version, reason and status are committed in the same audit transaction.

Tab-local drafts, verified session generations, native profile Save/Cancel/Escape, canonical uncertain-command retention and acknowledged success results now survive authorized in-tab navigation. Authorization denial invalidates older reads before private data can return. The existing live room transport remains separately verified; fixture browser UI evidence does not establish the full real private-push player-count matrix.

1	# Wordpairs Content Moderation Plan
2	
3	Current release override, 28 October 2026: [guest game and GitHub admin PWA](admin_pwa_release.md)
4	disables public nominations, category submissions and role delegation. Existing
5	case/history and catalog moderation remain available only to the verified GitHub
6	owner sharpninja. The earlier multi-role community workflow below is retained as
7	historical design, not an active public entry point in this release.
8	
9	**Status:** Implemented in Phase 5 and extended by the reviewed administration/ACL pages on 27 October 2026
10	**Requirements baseline:** `word_association_game_requirements.md` v2.6  
11	**Implementation sequence:** `implementation_plan.md`  
12	**Current scope:** player nominations and category/pair suggestions; no public chat
13	
14	## 1. Purpose and scope
15	
16	This plan defines the workflow, data boundaries, reviewer experience, audit trail, and test coverage for user-submitted candidate answers and category/pair suggestions. It supports FR-16–FR-17 and AC-16–AC-19 and AC-47 in the requirements. Requirements v2.6 establishes nomination thresholds, moderator roles, reasoned decisions, one senior-moderator appeal, and catalog activation gates; retention and audit details are also fixed there. The new public landing page (FR-22/AC-43/AC-50) may show leaderboard labels and lobby summaries; this plan treats those as a separate public projection, not moderation data. It does not publish user submissions or introduce a public chat feature.
17	
18	There are two related but different flows:
19	
20	- **Candidate nomination:** a player who solves during the no-hint stage nominates a word for possible inclusion in a future answer pool. A candidate must meet the approved nomination threshold and pass moderation; even then it cannot be played until editors create a complete curated word-pair record.
21	- **Category and pair suggestion:** a player who has ten lifetime wins on one stable profile proposes one relationship category and exactly three pairs. Review and approval do not make those pairs playable until each record and the category background are complete and the curated catalog passes validation.
22	
23	The moderation process reviews content quality and suitability. It does not resolve the gameplay requirement questions, choose accepted-answer policy, or automatically promote content because it received votes. The curated catalog remains the only source of playable prompts, answers, hints, accepted alternatives, and background references.
24	
25	## 2. Product principles
26	
27	1. **Human decision for publication:** automation may check formatting, duplicates, and completeness, but only an authorized reviewer can approve user content for editorial use.
28	2. **Approval is not publication:** an approved nomination is only eligible for curation; an approved suggestion is only eligible for catalog preparation. Curated records need a separate editorial completion and release step.
29	3. **Explicit, consistent reasons:** every rejection, request for revision, and approval records a reason code and reviewer rationale. Apply the same policy to comparable submissions.
30	4. **Privacy by default:** do not expose nominator identities or private guesses to other players. The public game need not reveal reviewer identity or internal notes. Collect only the information needed to enforce eligibility and audit decisions.
31	5. **No paid moderation dependency:** use deterministic validation and human review. Do not make a paid language-model, moderation API, or other metered service a launch dependency. A later optional classifier would only prioritize/flag, never silently approve or reject.
32	6. **Separation of duties:** a submitter cannot approve their own submission. The authorized moderator/editor role is distinct from the ordinary player role. If one owner performs several roles in an early release, preserve the audit trail and expose that the review was self-administered.
33	7. **Decision records are durable:** retain an auditable history of threshold changes, reviews, status transitions, and catalog linkage. A moderation action must not rewrite nomination history.
34	8. **Keep live play safe and predictable:** only complete, approved content may enter a published catalog version. Nominations and suggestions never alter an active match.
35	
36	## 3. Policy boundary and content standards
37	
38	The requirements specify product outcomes. The content checklist below is operational guidance for human reviewers and does not change AC expectations; technical review interfaces and permissions are approved in Phase 0.
39	
40	### 3.1 Reviewer checklist
41	
42	| Review dimension | Approve when | Return/reject when |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| Eligibility | The submitter satisfies the approved gameplay/win rule; the record has required fields. | The submitter is ineligible, the nomination is from a hinted solve, or the submission is structurally incomplete. |
45	| Relationship | The prompt and answer form a clear, defensible relationship in the selected category; the relation is understandable without private context. | The pair is arbitrary, misleading, ambiguous, or categorized incorrectly. |
46	| Accuracy | Names, dates, titles, spelling, and claims are accurate enough for the approved content standard. Reviewer records a reference for disputed or non-obvious factual claims. | Material factual error cannot be corrected or the pair depends on an unsupported assertion. |
47	| Distinctiveness | The candidate adds useful variety and is not an accidental normalized duplicate of an existing candidate, pair, category, or alias. | It duplicates existing content without adding a useful accepted alternative. |
48	| Playability | The answer has a clear accepted-answer policy; three useful ordered hints can be written without revealing the answer too early; the prompt is solvable at the intended difficulty. | No fair prompt/hint sequence can be created or a hint leaks the target before its stage. |
49	| Audience and harm | Content meets the general-audience suitability baseline in the v2.6 requirements. Reviewers can flag slurs, targeted abuse, threats, personal data, sexual content, or other sensitive content for restricted review. | It violates the approved safety policy or targets a private person with abusive content. |
50	| Rights and attribution | Text/artwork can be used with appropriate permissions/notices and the pair does not depend on copying protected material beyond an approved use. | Required permission is absent, attribution is impossible, or a proposed asset conflicts with GPL distribution requirements. |
51	| Category quality | The category name is distinct, describable, and supports a coherent set of pairs and a suitable background. | It is a duplicate, too broad to guide content, or cannot be represented safely and consistently. |
52	
53	### 3.2 Resolved moderation policy
54	
55	Requirements v2.6 fixes the policy: ten unique profiles trigger review; each profile may nominate a candidate once and submit at most one candidate per eligible no-hint solve; an independent Content Moderator approves or rejects with a reason; one appeal may be submitted to a Senior Moderator; ten lifetime wins unlock one open category suggestion containing exactly three pairs. Approval does not publish incomplete content. The implementation follows the approved Phase 0 role checks, versioned state transitions and same-transaction audit contract, with separate PostgreSQL evidence for database guarantees.
56	
57	Candidate matching uses the requirements' Unicode NFKC, trim, internal-whitespace collapse and case-insensitive normalization while preserving punctuation. The submitted spelling is retained separately for reviewer display. Public aliases and leaderboard opt-out follow FR-22. Rejected or pending user content is not public or playable. The requirements' retention schedule governs audit, idempotency and outbox records; no raw incorrect guesses are persisted.
58	
59	## 4. Roles and permissions
60	
61	The 27 October 2026 [admin/ACL extension](admin_acl_design.md) makes the roles operational. Its permission matrix supersedes the earlier proposed separation between moderator and content-editor accounts below: moderators and senior moderators can curate approved cases and author/edit catalog pairs; administrators additionally manage role grants and revocations. Direct editorial saves require a reason and create immutable versions. Community case review and independent appeals remain mandatory for the community workflow. The admin role does not waive proposer/original-reviewer independence.
62	
63	Bootstrap administrators are defined by the server-only `WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS` allowlist. Other privileges are persisted in PostgreSQL, audited and checked on the server. Configured administrator authority cannot be removed through the UI, and concurrent changes cannot remove every effective administrator. There is no public privilege-escalation or role-bootstrap endpoint.
64	
65	| Role | Allowed actions | Not allowed |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| Player / submitter | Submit an eligible nomination; submit an unlocked category/pair proposal; view own submission status and public decision reason; submit one appeal to a Senior Moderator. | See another player's private nomination identity, internal reviewer notes, or unresolved drafts; approve own content; edit the live catalog. |
68	| Moderator | Review eligible cases; approve or reject with a reason; curate complete approved proposals; author/edit word pairs and hints as immutable versions; exclude content from future rounds; inspect content history. | Change vote history or scores, approve own submission, resolve appeals, assign roles, or erase audit history. |
69	| Senior moderator | All moderator permissions plus independent reasoned appeal resolution. | Resolve an appeal of own submission or original decision, assign roles, or erase audit history. |
70	| Administrator | All senior-moderator permissions plus audited role grants/revocations and user-directory access. | Bypass proposer/original-reviewer independence, remove configured administrator authority through the UI, remove the final effective administrator, or erase audit history. |
71	| System | Validate structure, normalize duplicate keys, count eligible votes/wins, create queue cases, enforce status transitions, and record immutable events. | Make final content suitability decisions unless a specific deterministic rule has been approved. |
72	
73	The landing page uses generated public aliases and honors profile opt-out as specified in v2.6. Do not expose moderator-only fields or nomination histories as leaderboard data. If player-selected labels are used publicly, the display-name policy must define reserved/prohibited strings, report/removal handling, and how a disabled label is represented. These choices belong to the landing-page decision register, not the nomination review queue unless the product owner explicitly connects the workflows.
74	
75	Moderator and senior-moderator authority is defined by the v2.6 policy; role storage and server-side assignment are technical design items. All privileged actions require server-side role checks; hiding an admin link in the browser is not authorization. Use the least-privilege service key only server-side. Require re-authentication or additional confirmation for permanent deletion and emergency disablement if supported by the approved identity design.
76	
77	## 5. Submission lifecycle
78	
79	### 5.1 Candidate nomination lifecycle
80	
81	1. **Eligibility check:** on submission, the server verifies the player identity, active game/round, accepted no-hint solve, one-time/duplicate policy, and allowed submission window.
82	2. **Input handling:** retain the original spelling for display; derive a normalized comparison key using the v2.6 normalization rules; reject empty, excessive-length, malformed, or control-character input. Do not put raw text in general logs.
83	3. **Duplicate/threshold handling:** associate the nomination with the canonical candidate record or create a pending candidate. Apply the unique-profile and one-candidate-per-eligible-solve rules transactionally. Recheck threshold at commit to avoid double counting.
84	4. **Pre-review state:** keep below-threshold candidates out of playable content and out of public room views. Flag suspected personal data or prohibited content for restricted review; flagged content remains hidden from public projections and is not playable.
85	5. **Review queue:** once threshold and required eligibility rules pass, create exactly one active moderation case. Store the threshold snapshot and nomination count that triggered the case; subsequent votes remain auditable and do not duplicate the queue item.
86	6. **Human decision:** reviewer inspects original/normalized text, duplicate candidates, counts, game context, and references. Reviewer chooses `approved_for_curation`, `needs_revision`, `rejected`, or a restricted `escalated` state 
87	7. **Curation:** approval marks the candidate eligible for future-pool curation, not playable. Editor creates a complete pair with prompt, category, target, three hints, accepted answers, and background; content validation must pass.
88	8. **Catalog release:** only a reviewed catalog version with complete records is deployed. Record which moderation case and source candidate led to the pair. Never alter a published active match's content snapshot.
89	
90	Open a moderation case when the ten-unique-profile threshold is reached. Approval and threshold are independent eligibility gates: neither alone makes a candidate eligible for curation.
91	
92	### 5.2 Category-and-pair suggestion lifecycle
93	
94	1. Check the ten-lifetime-wins stable-profile rule on the server; do not trust a client-supplied win total.
95	2. Accept one category proposal with exactly three pair proposals as a single submission transaction. Enforce size limits and field validation for each proposed pair.
96	3. Snapshot the eligibility evidence, proposer, category label, three pair records, submission time, and version. The proposer may not edit the submitted version in place.
97	4. Run deterministic validation: duplicate category/name, pair duplicates, missing fields, invalid hint count/order, invalid category/background references, prohibited markup/control characters, and content-size bounds.
98	5. Place the complete submission into review. Moderator considers the category and all three pairs together, with the option to request revision of the whole package or individual pairs.
99	6. On approval, create an editorial work item. Editors verify the relationship, factuality, answer alternatives, three hints, and artwork/background rights; a category background asset is not user-uploaded at launch under the current requirements.
100	7. Validate the finished catalog record and include it in a versioned catalog release. Only then is any proposed pair playable.
101	8. On rejection, preserve the case/reason and provide only approved public feedback. A resubmission is a new version linked to the prior case, not destructive overwrite.
102	
103	### 5.3 Case states
104	
105	Keep nomination eligibility, moderation review, editorial completion, and playability as separate dimensions rather than one overloaded status field.
106	
107	| Dimension | Suggested states | Meaning |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| Nomination threshold | `collecting`, `threshold_met`, `withdrawn`, `closed` | Counts and availability; threshold is not an approval. |
110	| Moderation case | `not_queued`, `queued`, `in_review`, `needs_revision`, `approved`, `rejected`, `escalated`, `appealed`, `closed` | Human decision lifecycle. Only the proposer may file one appeal of a rejected decision. A distinct Senior Moderator records a reasoned uphold or overturn; overturn permits curation only and never activates content. |
111	| Editorial curation | `not_started`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `complete` | Whether a complete validated game record exists. |
112	| Catalog availability | `not_playable`, `scheduled`, `active`, `disabled` | Release-level state; only `active` content can enter a newly created round. |
113	
114	Transitions must be explicit and permission-checked. A change in one dimension cannot imply a transition in another: `threshold_met` does not mean `approved`; `approved` does not mean `complete`; `complete` does not mean `active` until a catalog release includes it.
115	
116	## 6. Data and audit design
117	
118	Finalize physical schema during architecture planning. The following logical records are required for reliable enforcement:
119	
120	- **Candidate:** stable ID, original display form, normalized comparison key/version, creation time, current threshold state, aggregate eligible-voter count, and current moderation/editorial pointers.
121	- **Nomination:** candidate ID, player/profile ID, source game/round ID, eligibility evidence, submitted form, timestamp, and idempotency key. Uniqueness constraints encode the approved repeat-vote policy.
122	- **Category/pair submission:** submitter, eligibility evidence, immutable version number, category proposal, exactly three proposed pair objects, timestamps, and linked prior revision/case where relevant.
123	- **Moderation case:** target type/ID/version, state, assigned reviewer, priority/flags, reason code, reviewer rationale, created/updated/closed times, and appeal linkage.
124	- **Moderation event:** append-only actor, action, previous/new state, timestamp, policy version, reason code, and non-secret metadata. Do not store complete OAuth tokens or raw guesses in the audit record.
125	- **Editorial item/catalog record:** source case/candidate, final pair/category fields, content provenance/reference notes, approval status, catalog version, and activation/disable history.
126	
127	Enforce uniqueness and threshold counting in database transactions or a server-controlled database function so concurrent votes cannot cross the threshold inconsistently. Add row-level security that denies client-side direct updates to moderation states, thresholds, and catalog publication. Use service operations for authorized review actions. Keep a small, explicit list of public status fields; internal notes, risk flags, voter identities, and staff data remain private.
128	
129	The resolved retention schedule is one year for audit events, seven days for published outbox rows, and until 30 days after room close for idempotency results. Raw incorrect guesses are not persisted. Moderation candidate/submission records retain only the content and identity linkage required for review and audit; access is restricted and deletion/pseudonymization follows applicable account-removal requirements without erasing the fact of a decision.
130	
131	## 7. Moderator operations
132	
133	### 7.1 Queue and review procedure
134	
135	1. Open the case from the authenticated moderation interface; verify the target type, current version, eligibility evidence, duplicate search, and reason the case entered review.
136	2. Confirm no concurrent reviewer has completed or changed the case; use optimistic version checking when saving.
137	3. Review each checklist dimension from Section 3. Add factual references for claims where accuracy is not common knowledge. Mark uncertainty as a question or request for revision rather than inventing a fact.
138	4. Select a reason code and write brief, actionable rationale. Keep private operational notes separate from the submitter-facing explanation.
139	5. Save the decision atomically; system records reviewer ID/time, case version, policy version, old/new status, and rationale. Reject stale writes and preserve the current case state.
140	6. If approved, create/link the editorial task and explain that approval is not publication. If rejected or returned, notify the submitter with the approved public reason and next permitted action.
141	7. For escalated/high-risk content, hide the submission from ordinary player views pending a second authorized review. Preserve evidence with restricted access; do not quote the material publicly.
142	
143	### 7.2 Queue ordering and workload
144	
145	Use FIFO order as the simple default, with explicit escalation for risk flags, appeals, and approaching operational review age. Do not reward controversial or harmful content with visibility or popularity ranking. Display age, queue reason, candidate type, and current state; do not show personally identifying player details unless necessary to make a decision.
146	
147	Because this is a free-tier, small-scope project, the initial approach is an owner-operated manual queue rather than paid moderation SaaS. Define a target review window only after expected submission volume and reviewer availability are known. The UI should state that review can take time; do not promise an unsupported SLA. Alerting may use existing free project email or a manual queue check, but the release cannot depend on a paid notification provider.
148	
149	### 7.3 Appeals, revision, and emergency disablement
150	
151	Only the proposer may submit one appeal after rejection. The system assigns it to a Senior Moderator distinct from the original reviewer; that reviewer records a reasoned uphold or overturn. Uphold keeps the rejection. Overturn moves the case to approved-for-curation, and still does not add content to the playable pool. A closed appeal cannot be resubmitted. Preserve every version, command ID, actor, decision, reason, and transition in the transactional audit. Stale versions are rejected and retries with the same command ID return the canonical result.
152	
153	Provide a privileged `disable` operation for active catalog content that is found to be harmful, inaccurate, rights-infringing, or otherwise unsuitable. It blocks inclusion in future rounds and future catalog releases; it cannot rewrite already completed match history. An active match continues using its content snapshot; disablement prevents selection in future rounds and catalog releases. Record actor, reason, time, affected catalog version, and whether the content remains visible in historical summaries.
154	
155	## 8. Moderation controls and acceptance-criteria traceability
156	
157	AC-16 through AC-19 and AC-47 cover catalog completeness, nomination thresholds/moderation, category-suggestion unlock, authorization and audit. The controls below detail implementation of those accepted requirements and technical safeguards. Additional product behavior is out of scope until explicitly added to requirements and the traceability matrix.
158	
159	| Control | Given/when/then contract |
160	|---|---|
161	| **M-01 Role enforcement** | Given a player without a moderator/editor role, when they call a review, edit, or catalog activation operation, then the server rejects it and records no state change. |
162	| **M-02 Nomination uniqueness** | Given the approved vote-counting policy, when duplicate or repeat nominations arrive concurrently, then the candidate count reflects only eligible distinct votes and remains correct after retries. |
163	| **M-03 Independent gates** | Given a nomination meets the threshold but lacks approval, or has approval but is below threshold, when future-pool eligibility is calculated, then it remains ineligible. |
164	| **M-04 Review audit** | Given an authorized reviewer changes a case, when the transition commits, then an immutable event records actor, time, prior/new state, policy version, and reason while keeping internal notes private. |
165	| **M-05 No self-approval** | Given a submitter is also a moderator, when that person attempts to approve their own version, then approval is blocked or the separately approved self-review policy is applied and audited. |
166	| **M-06 Revision history** | Given a submitter revises a returned proposal, when the new version is reviewed, then the prior version and decisions remain auditable and the new version requires review. |
167	| **M-07 Catalog boundary** | Given approved content is incomplete or absent from an active catalog release, when a match selects content, then the record cannot be played. |
168	| **M-08 Restricted-content handling** | Given a submission triggers an approved sensitive-content flag, when it is escalated, then it is hidden from ordinary player views and accessible only to authorized reviewers. |
169	| **M-09 Disable active content** | Given an authorized editor disables a catalog item, when a new round starts, then the disabled item is excluded; historical match records remain stable. |
170	| **M-10 Privacy** | Given a player views a room or another player's status, when moderation data is returned, then voter identity, private notes, raw guesses, and staff-only flags are not exposed. |
171	
172	M-01 through M-10 are moderation-plan controls, not independent acceptance criteria. Trace applicable controls to AC-16–19/47; do not use additional controls to claim AC coverage.
173	
174	## 9. Mock-first test and implementation plan
175	
176	Moderation code follows the same Byrd Development Process v4 gates as the rest of Wordpairs. For each increment, tests for every applicable accepted AC are written first, validated against mocks/fakes, and only then can implementation begin. Maintain the AC/test matrix in `implementation_plan.md` and add moderation-specific test IDs when the policies are approved.
177	
178	| Increment | Scope | Required mock-first cases |
179	|---|---|---|
180	| **M0 — Approved policy and interface baseline** | Requirements v2.6 and the Phase 0 interface contract already approve standards, roles, thresholds, state transitions, normalization, appeal limits, retention, and database boundaries. | No production code. Test cases use fake role verification, candidate repository, policy version, threshold counter, clock, and audit writer; all 45 ACs pass the global mock gate before implementation. |
181	| **M1 — Eligibility and nomination capture** | Enforce no-hint solve, nomination window, input limits, normalized candidate key, duplicate policy, and transactional vote count. | Eligible/ineligible player; no-hint vs hinted solve; duplicate spelling; Unicode/case/whitespace variants; repeat attempt; concurrent threshold race; idempotent retry; invalid/control/oversize input. Cover AC-17 and approved M-02. |
182	| **M2 — Threshold and moderation queue** | Maintain candidate gate states and create a queue case under the approved before/after-threshold policy. | 9/10 boundary, vote removed/invalidated policy, approved-but-below-threshold, threshold-without-approval, concurrent queue creation, no duplicate cases, restricted flag access. Cover AC-18 and approved M-03/M-08. |
183	| **M3 — Review permissions and audit** | Role-guard review actions; implement approved state transitions, reason codes, optimistic concurrency, private/public views, and immutable audit. | Player denial; moderator permitted; self-approval rule; stale case version; invalid transition; private-note non-disclosure; audit commit/rollback behavior. Cover approved M-01/M-04/M-05/M-10. |
184	| **M4 — Revision, appeal, and editorial handoff** | Implement approved revision/appeal flow and curation item creation. | Old versions retained; revision re-enters review; appeal assigned appropriately; rejection does not publish; approval creates editorial task but not playable content. Cover AC-18 and approved M-06/M-07. |
185	| **M5 — Category/pair proposals** | Enforce win-unlock, exactly three pairs, package review, and catalog/editor handoff. | Below/at win threshold; client-forged wins rejected; wrong pair count; incomplete record; duplicate category/pairs; approval still not active/playable. Cover AC-19, AC-16, and approved M-01/M-07. |
186	| **M6 — Disablement and moderation integration** | Implement catalog disablement and integrate moderated content with release versioning and active-match snapshots. | Disabled item excluded from new rounds; in-progress match follows approved snapshot rule; history unchanged; audit and catalog version linkage. Cover approved M-09 and regression AC-16/18/19. |
187	
188	Use fake clocks, deterministic IDs, repository fakes, transaction fakes, and event capture. Mocks must reflect public contracts rather than copy the business rule under test. After unit tests pass, add Supabase migration/RLS/transaction integration tests using local or disposable Staging data. Browser tests cover submitter and reviewer views with network interception and synthetic data. No automated test uses Production credentials or paid moderation services.
189	
190	## 10. Security, privacy, and abuse controls
191	
192	- Enforce submitter identity and eligibility on the server; ignore client-supplied profile IDs, win counts, solve stages, vote totals, or moderator roles.
193	- Rate-limit submissions and review mutations using a design compatible with Free quotas. Do not reveal if a specific player nominated or reported a word. Define limits as approved policy and test boundaries.
194	- Normalize only for comparison; do not discard original spelling before review. Guard against Unicode confusables, hidden bidirectional controls, control characters, markup injection, and excessively long text.
195	- Render submissions as text, never unsanitized HTML. Escape all moderator rationale and user-facing decision text. Avoid embedding user text into logs, URLs, or metric labels.
196	- Keep candidate status and reviewer data out of public room Realtime channels. Publish only explicitly whitelisted events to authorized recipients.
197	- Protect moderation/admin routes with server-side authorization, CSRF protection appropriate to the chosen route model, rate limiting, and audit logging. Use service credentials only in the server runtime.
198	- Minimize retained personal data and apply the v2.6 retention schedule. Never retain raw incorrect guesses for moderation; the game requirement says guess text remains private.
199	- Treat suspected threats, personal information, or rights complaints as restricted cases; suppress public display while review is pending
200	- Do not assume a content filter can make final policy judgments. Any classifier is a future, optional triage aid that must have its own cost, bias, privacy, accuracy, and appeal review.
201	
202	## 11. Moderation quality and operational metrics
203	
204	Metrics should measure process health without turning vote count into a popularity contest or exposing individuals:
205	
206	- Counts by candidate/suggestion status and queue age.
207	- Median review time and backlog size; number of revision requests, approvals, rejections, escalations, and appeals.
208	- Duplicate rate, incomplete-submission rate, catalog-validation failure rate, and content disabled after publication.
209	- Threshold-to-review transition failures and concurrent count reconciliation errors.
210	- Privacy/security incidents, unauthorized actions blocked, and audit-write failures.
211	
212	Do not publish nominee identities or rank candidate words by vote totals. Set targets only after observed volume is known. A review backlog must not automatically approve pending submissions; pending content remains unplayable.
213	
214	## 12. Rollout and completion gates
215	
216	1. **Baseline review:** verify the resolved v2.6 policy is reflected in the moderation interface, state model and test specifications.
217	2. **Requirements update:** add requirements and acceptance criteria only if scope changes; update and render relevant diagrams as SVG when workflow topology changes.
218	3. **Design review:** approve data model, authorization matrix, state machine, public API, privacy boundaries, queue UX, catalog handoff, and audit schema before coding.
219	4. **Mock-first tests:** map every active AC to test IDs; validate all tests for the increment against mocks before production implementation. Maintain 100% active AC coverage and green prior increments.
220	5. **Staging trial:** use synthetic submissions and test moderator/editor accounts; verify role checks, queue transitions, audit history, privacy projections, and catalog release linkage.
221	6. **Release gate:** confirm no unreviewed or incomplete user proposal is playable; review dependencies/license/attribution and protect the Production catalog migration. Keep content enablement separate from deployment.
222	7. **Operations review:** inspect queue health and audit integrity; respond to flags using approved policy; review policy effectiveness after actual use and revise requirements through the normal change process.
223	
224	Moderation is complete for a release only when every approved moderation criterion passes, sensitive/internal data is not exposed, audit events are verifiable, approved content cannot skip curation/catalog gates, and moderators can act without accessing Production secrets or raw private gameplay data beyond what the approved review policy requires.
225	
226	## 13. Resolved policy and remaining technical review
227	
228	The product policy checklist is resolved by requirements v2.6; there are no open product decisions for nomination count, nomination eligibility, moderation roles, appeal count, lifetime-win scope, public aliases, or retention. Phase 0 approved the technical role assignment, authorization/RLS, state transitions, concurrent threshold enforcement, audit transaction boundaries, and test interfaces. Phase 5 implemented the community workflow; the [administration/ACL extension](admin_acl_design.md) supplies the dedicated pages and audited role management. Real database guarantees remain separate TR integration evidence.
229
